translations.literal: Biographies 20 ○ Guo Yaoshi, son: Anguo; Yelü Tushan; Wuyan Huligai; Wuyan Wulibu; Xiao Gong; Wanyan Xibuzhu; Geshilie Hula; Yelü Shu; Guo Qizhong; Wusun Elun; Yanzhan Mendu; Pusan Huntan; Zheng Jianchong; Wugulun Sanhe; Yila Wen; Xiao Zhonggong, son: Gong; Xiao Zhongxuan; Gao Song; Hailing's sons Guangying, Yuanshou, Shensi Abu; Guangyang
translations.idiomatic: Biography 20 — Guo Yaoshi; his son Anguo; Yelü Tushan; Wuyan Huligai; Wuyan Wulibu; Xiao Gong; Wanyan Xibuzhu; Geshilie Hula; Yelü Shu; Guo Qizhong; Wusun Elun; Yanzhan Mendu; Pusan Huntan; Zheng Jianchong; Wugulun Sanhe; Yila Wen; Xiao Zhonggong and his son Gong; Xiao Zhongxuan; Gao Song; Emperor Hailing's sons Guangying, Yuanshou, and Shensi Abu; and Guangyang

sentences.zh: 郭藥師

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi

sentences.zh: 郭藥師，渤海鐵州人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi was a man of Tiezhou in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi was a native of Tiezhou in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 遼國募遼東人為兵，使報怨於女直，號曰「怨軍」，藥師為其渠帥。

translations.literal: The Liao state recruited men from eastern Liaodong as soldiers to take revenge on the Jurchens; they were called the "Army of Grievance," and Yaoshi was their chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao recruited troops from eastern Liaodong to strike at the Jurchens; this force was called the "Army of Grievance," and Yaoshi served as its commander.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古攻顯州，敗藥師於城下。

translations.literal: Wolugu attacked Xianzhou and defeated Yaoshi beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wolugu attacked Xianzhou and routed Yaoshi before the city.

sentences.zh: 遼帝亡保天德，耶律捏里自立，改「怨軍」為「常勝軍」，擢藥師諸衛上將軍。

translations.literal: The Liao emperor fled and took refuge at Tiande; Yelü Nieli declared himself ruler, changed the "Army of Grievance" to the "Ever-Victorious Army," and promoted Yaoshi to General-in-Chief of the Various Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor fled to Tiande, Yelü Nieli seized power, renamed the Army of Grievance the Ever-Victorious Army, and promoted Yaoshi to general-in-chief of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 捏里死，其妻蕭妃稱制，藥師以涿、易二州歸於宋。

translations.literal: When Nieli died, his wife the Lady Xiao assumed regency; Yaoshi surrendered the two prefectures of Zhuo and Yi to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: After Nieli's death, his wife Lady Xiao ruled as regent, and Yaoshi surrendered the prefectures of Zhuo and Yi to the Song.

sentences.zh: 藥師以宋兵六千人奄至燕京，甄五臣以五千人奪迎春門，皆入城。

translations.literal: Yaoshi led six thousand Song troops in a sudden advance on Yanjing; Zhen Wuchen with five thousand men seized the Yingchun Gate, and all entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshi led six thousand Song troops in a surprise march on Yanjing; Zhen Wuchen stormed the Yingchun Gate with five thousand men, and both forces entered the city.

sentences.zh: 蕭妃令閉城門與宋兵巷戰。

translations.literal: Lady Xiao ordered the city gates shut and fought the Song troops in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao had the gates closed and fought the Song army street by street within the city.

sentences.zh: 藥師大敗，失馬步走，逾城以免。

translations.literal: Yaoshi suffered a great defeat, lost his horse, fled on foot, and escaped over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshi was routed, lost his mount, fled on foot, and climbed over the wall to escape.

sentences.zh: 宋人猶厚賞之。

translations.literal: The Song still rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Song court nevertheless rewarded him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 子 安國

translations.literal: Son: Anguo
translations.idiomatic: His son Anguo

sentences.zh: 郭安國，藥師子也。

translations.literal: Guo Anguo was the son of Yaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Anguo was Guo Yaoshi's son.

sentences.zh: 累遷奉國上將軍、南京副留守。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to General-in-Chief Who Upholds the State and Deputy Military Commissioner of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to general-in-chief who upholds the state and deputy military commissioner of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，南京大內火，海陵使右司郎中梁钅求、同知安武軍節度事王全按問失火狀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, fire broke out in the inner palace of the Southern Capital; Hailing dispatched Right Department Director Liang Qiu and Vice Commissioner of the Anwu Military Circuit Wang Quan to investigate the circumstances of the fire.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3 (1155), the inner palace of the Southern Capital burned; Emperor Hailing sent Right Department Director Liang Qiu and Vice Commissioner of the Anwu Military Circuit Wang Quan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 留守馮長寧、都轉運使左瀛各杖一百，除名。

translations.literal: The military commissioner Feng Changning and the metropolitan transport commissioner Zuo Ying were each flogged one hundred strokes and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Feng Changning and Metropolitan Transport Commissioner Zuo Ying each received a hundred strokes of the rod and were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 安國及留守判官大良順各杖八十，削三官。

translations.literal: Anguo and the military commissioner's judicial aide Dalangshun were each flogged eighty strokes and stripped of three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo and the commissioner's judicial aide Dalangshun each received eighty strokes and were demoted three ranks.

sentences.zh: 火起處勾當官南京兵馬都指揮使吳浚杖一百五十，除名。

translations.literal: Wu Jun, the duty officer at the site where the fire started and commander of all troops and horses of the Southern Capital, was flogged one hundred fifty strokes and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jun, the officer on duty where the fire began and commander of the Southern Capital's forces, received a hundred and fifty strokes and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 失火位押宿兵吏十三人並斬。

translations.literal: The thirteen soldiers and clerks on night watch at the place of the fire were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: All thirteen soldiers and clerks on night watch where the fire had broken out were executed.

sentences.zh: 諭之曰：「朕非以宮闕壯麗也。

translations.literal: He instructed them, saying: "It is not that I care about the splendor of the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: He told them: "I do not care about the grandeur of the palace.

sentences.zh: 自即位以來，欲巡省河南，汝等不知防慎，致外方奸細，燒延殆盡。

translations.literal: Since I took the throne I have wished to tour and inspect Henan; you did not know how to take precautions, so that enemy agents from outside came and the fire spread until nearly everything was burned.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession I have planned to tour Henan, yet you failed to guard against infiltration, allowing enemy agents to set a blaze that nearly destroyed everything.

sentences.zh: 本欲處爾等死罪，特以舊人寬貸之。

translations.literal: I originally intended to sentence you to death, but because you are old associates I have shown special leniency.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to put you to death, but as longtime followers I have spared you.

sentences.zh: 押宿人兵法當處死，疑此輩容隱奸細，故皆斬也。」

translations.literal: Those on night watch are by military law subject to execution; I suspect this group concealed enemy agents, and therefore they were all beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Night watchmen are liable to death under military law; I suspect they sheltered enemy agents, and that is why they were all executed."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：郭藥師者，遼之餘孽，宋之厲階，金之功臣也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Guo Yaoshi was a remnant of Liao, a stepping-stone to disaster for Song, and a meritorious minister of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Guo Yaoshi was a survivor of Liao, the means by which Song brought ruin upon itself, and a meritorious servant of Jin.

sentences.zh: 以一臣之身而為三國之禍福，如是其不侔也。

translations.literal: That a single minister's person could be the fortune and misfortune of three states — how unequal such things are!
translations.idiomatic: That one man's career could shape the fate of three kingdoms shows how disproportionate such influence can be.

sentences.zh: 魏公叔痤勸其君殺衛鞅，豈無所見歟！

translations.literal: Duke Gongshu of Wei urged his lord to kill Wei Yang — was there not some insight in that!
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Gongshu of Wei urged his ruler to kill Wei Yang, did he not see something worth heeding!

sentences.zh: 耶律塗山

translations.literal: Yelü Tushan
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Tushan

sentences.zh: 耶律塗山，系出遙輦氏，在遼世為顯族。

translations.literal: Yelü Tushan was descended from the Yaolian clan and was a prominent family in Liao times.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Tushan traced his line to the Yaolian clan and belonged to a distinguished Liao family.

sentences.zh: 塗山仕至金吾衛大將軍、遙里相溫。

translations.literal: Tushan served to the rank of General of the Golden Crow Guard and yaoli xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan rose to general of the Golden Crow Guard and yaoli xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 遼帝奔天德，塗山以所部降，宗翰承制授尚書，為西北路招討使。

translations.literal: When the Liao emperor fled to Tiande, Tushan surrendered with his command; Zonghan, acting under imperial authority, appointed him Director of the Imperial Secretariat and made him pacification commissioner of the Northwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor fled to Tiande, Tushan surrendered with his troops; Zonghan, exercising imperial authority, appointed him director of the secretariat and pacification commissioner of the Northwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宗翰伐宋，塗山率本部為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Zonghan campaigned against Song, Tushan led his own command as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan invaded Song, Tushan led his command as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至汾州，遇宋將折家軍，請濟師並力破之。

translations.literal: At Fenzhou he encountered the Song general's Zhe family army and requested reinforcements to join forces and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: At Fenzhou he met the Zhe family's Song army and asked for reinforcements to crush it together.

sentences.zh: 從攻太原、隆德府，從入汴，克洛陽。

translations.literal: He followed in the attacks on Taiyuan and Longde Prefecture, followed in the entry into Bian, and captured Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the sieges of Taiyuan and Longde, entered Bianjing with the army, and captured Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及從婁室平陝右。

translations.literal: He also followed Loushi in pacifying the right of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Loushi in pacifying western Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 天會七年，授太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui he was appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 7 (1129) he was appointed junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒，年九十一。

translations.literal: He retired from office, died, and was ninety-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and died at the age of ninety-one.

sentences.zh: 正隆例贈特進、郜國公。

translations.literal: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was posthumously granted Special Advancement and the title Duke of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhenglong precedent he was posthumously granted special advancement and the title Duke of Gao.

sentences.zh: 烏延胡里改

translations.literal: Wuyan Huligai
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Huligai

sentences.zh: 烏延胡里改，曷懶路星顯水人也。

translations.literal: Wuyan Huligai was a man of Xingxianshui on the Yilan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Huligai was a native of Xingxianshui on the Yilan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 後授愛也窟謀克，因家焉。

translations.literal: Later he was granted the aiyeku company commander post and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed company commander of Aiyeku and settled there.

sentences.zh: 從闍母圍平州，有功。

translations.literal: He followed Zhamu in besieging Pingzhou and performed meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Zhamu at the siege of Pingzhou and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 及伐宋，圍汴，五謀克與宋兵萬人遇于城南，胡里改先馳擊敗之，元帥府遂賞良馬一匹。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Song and besieged Bian, five company commanders encountered ten thousand Song troops south of the city; Huligai charged first and defeated them, and the marshal's headquarters thereupon rewarded him with one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Song and the siege of Bian, five company commanders met ten thousand Song troops south of the city; Huligai led the charge and routed them, and headquarters rewarded him with a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 天會五年，攻宗城縣，敵棄城走恩州，胡里改追殺千餘人，獲車四百兩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhui he attacked Zongcheng County; the enemy abandoned the city and fled to Enzhou; Huligai pursued and killed more than a thousand men and captured four hundred carts.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 5 (1127) he attacked Zongcheng County; the enemy abandoned the city and fled toward Enzhou; Huligai pursued, killing over a thousand men and seizing four hundred carts.

sentences.zh: 帥府賞牛三十頭、馬一匹。

translations.literal: The marshal's headquarters rewarded him with thirty head of cattle and one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters rewarded him with thirty cattle and one horse.

sentences.zh: 七年，討泰山群盜，平之，毀其營柵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he suppressed the bandit gangs of Mount Tai, pacified them, and destroyed their camps and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he suppressed the bandits of Mount Tai, pacified the region, and razed their camps.

sentences.zh: 兗州群寇三千餘保據山險，胡里改複破之。

translations.literal: More than three thousand bandits of Yanzhou held mountain strongholds; Huligai again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Over three thousand Yanzhou bandits held mountain strongholds; Huligai defeated them as well.

sentences.zh: 賞牛二十二頭、馬四匹。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with twenty-two head of cattle and four horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with twenty-two cattle and four horses.

sentences.zh: 八年，攻廬州，至柘皋鎮，胡里改領甲士三十為前鋒，執宋所遣持書與劉四廂錡者七人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he attacked Luzhou; at Zhegao Town, Huligai led thirty armored soldiers as vanguard and seized seven men whom Song had sent bearing letters to Liu Yue of the Fourth Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he attacked Luzhou; at Zhegao, Huligai led thirty armored men as vanguard and captured seven Song messengers bound for Liu Yue's Fourth Commandery.

sentences.zh: 複以先鋒軍攻和州，比至含山縣五里，獲甲士二人，乃知宋三將將兵且至。

translations.literal: Again with the vanguard he attacked Hezhou; when he had come within five li of Hanshan County he captured two armored soldiers and thus learned that three Song generals were leading troops and would soon arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Again leading the vanguard against Hezhou, within five li of Hanshan County he captured two soldiers and learned that three Song generals were advancing with an army.

sentences.zh: 胡里改伏其軍，遂獲姚觀察。

translations.literal: Huligai ambushed with his army and thereupon captured Inspector Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Huligai laid an ambush and captured Inspector Yao.

sentences.zh: 帥府賞馬二匹。

translations.literal: The marshal's headquarters rewarded him with two horses.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters rewarded him with two horses.

sentences.zh: 九年，定陝右，胡里改以所部遇敵千人，敗之，生擒甲士一人，盡得敵之虛實。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when western Shaanxi was pacified, Huligai with his command encountered a thousand enemy troops, defeated them, captured one armored soldier alive, and learned the enemy's full situation.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, during the pacification of western Shaanxi, Huligai met a thousand enemy troops with his command, routed them, took one soldier alive, and learned the enemy's full dispositions.

sentences.zh: 又從蒲魯渾徇地熙秦，敗敵兵二千于秦州，賞馬一匹。

translations.literal: He also followed Puluhun in ranging over the Xi-Qin region, defeated two thousand enemy troops at Qinzhou, and was rewarded with one horse.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Puluhun in operations across Xi-Qin, defeated two thousand enemy troops at Qinzhou, and received a horse as reward.

sentences.zh: 宋人屯襄陽府，監軍按補遣胡里改領四猛安往攻之。

translations.literal: The Song encamped at Xiangyang Prefecture; the supervising general Anbu dispatched Huligai to lead four meng'an units to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song army was encamped at Xiangyang; Supervising General Anbu sent Huligai with four meng'an units to attack them.

sentences.zh: 宋兵三千已渡江，方營壁壘，乘其未就，突戰破之。

translations.literal: Three thousand Song troops had already crossed the river and were just building ramparts and stockades; taking advantage before they were finished, he made a sudden assault and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand Song troops had crossed the river and were still building fortifications; he struck before their works were complete and routed them.

sentences.zh: 梁王宗弼複河南，將攻陳州，遣胡里改以甲士三十捕偵候人。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Zongbi recovered Henan and was about to attack Chenzhou; he sent Huligai with thirty armored soldiers to capture scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Liang Zongbi recovered Henan and prepared to attack Chenzhou; he sent Huligai with thirty armored men to seize scouts.

sentences.zh: 至蔡州西，遇兵八十餘，戰敗之，獲南頓縣令。

translations.literal: West of Caizhou he encountered more than eighty troops, defeated them in battle, and captured the magistrate of Nandun County.
translations.idiomatic: West of Caizhou he met some eighty enemy troops, defeated them, and captured the magistrate of Nandun County.

sentences.zh: 及攻陳州，夜將四更，忽聞敵開門潰走，胡里改亟領二謀克軍追及之，而猛安突葛速亦領軍繼至，大敗之。

translations.literal: When they attacked Chenzhou, in the night near the fourth watch they suddenly heard the enemy open the gates and flee in rout; Huligai urgently led two company-commander units in pursuit and caught up with them, while the meng'an Tugesu also led troops in support and arrived; they inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Chenzhou, near the fourth watch of the night the enemy suddenly broke and fled through the gates; Huligai hastily pursued with two company-commander units, and when Meng'an Tugesu arrived with reinforcements they inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，遷定遠大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 2 (1142) he was promoted to general who pacifies the distant.

sentences.zh: 八年，授臨洮少尹，兼熙秦路兵馬副都總管。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Junior Administrator of Lintao and concurrently Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Troops and Horses of the Xi-Qin Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed junior administrator of Lintao and deputy commander of the Xi-Qin circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 九年，改同知京兆尹，兼本路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Vice Administrator of Jingzhao and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of Troops and Horses of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became vice administrator of Jingzhao and commander of that circuit's forces.

sentences.zh: 天德改同知平陽尹，兼河東南路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In Tiande he was changed to Vice Administrator of Pingyang and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of Troops and Horses of the Hedong South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tiande reign he became vice administrator of Pingyang and commander of the Hedong South circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，改同知曷懶路總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan he was changed to Vice Commissioner of the Yilan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3 he became vice commissioner of the Yilan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，授胡里改節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading Huligai was appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 4 (1164) Huligai was appointed military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，改歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was changed to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Guide Army.

sentences.zh: 十年，移鎮顯德。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to garrison Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was reassigned to garrison Xiande.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 十九年，詔授其子五十六武功將軍，世襲本路婆朵火河謀克。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year an edict appointed his son Wushiliu as General of Martial Achievement and granted hereditary succession to the poduohuohe company commander post on this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year an edict appointed his son Wushiliu general of martial achievement and granted him hereditary succession to the poduohuohe company command on this circuit.

sentences.zh: 烏延吾里補

translations.literal: Wuyan Wulibu
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Wulibu

sentences.zh: 烏延吾里補，曷懶路禪嶺人也。

translations.literal: Wuyan Wulibu was a man of Chanling on the Yilan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Wulibu was a native of Chanling on the Yilan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 徙大名路。

translations.literal: His family was relocated to the Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was relocated to the Daming Circuit.

sentences.zh: 天會中，從其父達吉補隸元帥右監軍麾下。

translations.literal: During Tianhui he followed his father Dajibu in serving under the marshal's right supervising army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhui era he served under the marshal's right supervising army with his father Dajibu.

sentences.zh: 撻懶以事赴闕，以達吉補自隨。

translations.literal: Talan went to court on business and took Dajibu with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Talan went to the capital on official business, he took Dajibu along.

sentences.zh: 吾里補領其父謀克，從大軍攻滄州。

translations.literal: Wulibu took command of his father's company and followed the main army in attacking Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wulibu assumed his father's company command and joined the main army in the attack on Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 方夷濠隍，城中兵來拒，吾里補以本部擊卻之。

translations.literal: Just as the moat and ramparts were being leveled, troops from within the city came out to resist; Wulibu with his own command drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: As the moat and walls were being cleared, garrison troops sallied forth; Wulibu drove them back with his own command.

sentences.zh: 王師下青州，力戰有功，獲馬百匹以獻，降獲賊黨甚眾。

translations.literal: When the imperial army descended on Qingzhou he fought fiercely with merit, captured one hundred horses and presented them, and accepted the surrender and capture of a great many bandit partisans.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army advanced on Qingzhou he fought with distinction, presented a hundred captured horses, and took the surrender of many rebels.

sentences.zh: 青州戍將覿吉補以萊州兵眾，請濟于帥府。

translations.literal: The Qingzhou garrison general Dijibu, because Laizhou's troops were numerous, requested reinforcements from headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingzhou garrison commander Dijibu, facing a large Laizhou force, requested reinforcements from headquarters.

sentences.zh: 吾里補將十二謀克兵往救之。

translations.literal: Wulibu led twelve company-commander units to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Wulibu led twelve company-commander units to his relief.

sentences.zh: 遂降其四營，拔其一營，得戶四千。

translations.literal: Thereupon he induced four camps to surrender, stormed one camp, and obtained four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He induced four camps to surrender, stormed a fifth, and took four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又敗賊兵五萬於恩州，攻破其營，降戶五萬，獲牛畜萬餘。

translations.literal: He again defeated fifty thousand bandit troops at Enzhou, stormed their camp, accepted the surrender of fifty thousand households, and obtained more than ten thousand head of cattle and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated fifty thousand rebels at Enzhou, stormed their camp, accepted the surrender of fifty thousand households, and seized more than ten thousand head of cattle and livestock.

sentences.zh: 將至臨清縣，遇敵兵三千，又敗之，俘獲甚眾，生擒賊首以獻。

translations.literal: When he was about to reach Linqing County he encountered three thousand enemy troops, defeated them again, took many captives, and captured the bandit chief alive and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Near Linqing County he met three thousand enemy troops, defeated them, took many prisoners, and presented the captured rebel leader alive.

sentences.zh: 帥府嘉其功，以奴婢百、牛三十賞之。

translations.literal: Headquarters praised his achievement and rewarded him with one hundred slaves and servants and thirty cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters commended his achievements and rewarded him with a hundred servants and thirty cattle.

sentences.zh: 時覿吉補敗於恩州之境，吾里補複以兵四千往救之，破敵萬餘。

translations.literal: At that time Dijibu had been defeated in the Enzhou region; Wulibu again led four thousand troops to rescue him and defeated more than ten thousand enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Dijibu had been defeated near Enzhou, Wulibu again led four thousand men to his relief and routed more than ten thousand enemy troops.

sentences.zh: 宋兵十萬在單父間，總管宗室移剌屋選步卒一萬、騎兵四千往討之。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand Song troops were in the region of Shanfu; the commissioner, the imperial clansman Yila Wuxuan, selected ten thousand infantry and four thousand cavalry to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand Song troops were encamped near Shanfu; Commissioner Yila Wuxuan of the imperial clan led ten thousand infantry and four thousand cavalry against them.

sentences.zh: 吾里補領其親管謀克以從，遇敵先登，力戰有功。

translations.literal: Wulibu led the company commanders under his personal command in following; when they met the enemy he was first to ascend and fought fiercely with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wulibu led his personal company commanders in the campaign; he was first into battle and fought with distinction.

sentences.zh: 大軍經略密州，吾里補將兵二千為前鋒，遇敵萬人于高密，遂敗其眾，追至城下，殺戮殆盡，獲馬牛三千餘。

translations.literal: The main army conducted operations against Mizhou; Wulibu led two thousand troops as vanguard, encountered ten thousand enemy at Gaomi, thereupon defeated their host, pursued to beneath the city walls, and killed nearly all; he obtained more than three thousand horses and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: As the main army advanced on Mizhou, Wulibu led two thousand men as vanguard; at Gaomi he met ten thousand enemy, routed them, pursued to the walls, and slaughtered nearly the entire force, seizing more than three thousand horses and cattle.

sentences.zh: 吾里補與孛太欲敗賊王義軍十余萬于州南。

translations.literal: Wulibu and Botaiyu defeated Wang Yi's bandit army of more than a hundred thousand south of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wulibu and Botaiyu defeated Wang Yi's rebel army of over a hundred thousand south of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 是夜，賊兵數千來襲營，吾里補以兵橫擊走之。

translations.literal: That night several thousand bandit troops came to raid the camp; Wulibu struck them across their line of advance and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: That night several thousand rebels raided the camp; Wulibu struck them in flank and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 後從大軍攻楚、揚、通、泰等州。

translations.literal: Later he followed the main army in attacking Chu, Yang, Tong, Tai, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the main army in the conquest of Chu, Yang, Tong, Tai, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，襲其父世襲猛安，授甯遠大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he inherited his father's hereditary meng'an post and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 2 (1139) he inherited his father's hereditary meng'an command and was appointed general who pacifies the distant.

sentences.zh: 皇統七年，益以親管謀克。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huangtong he was additionally granted the personally commanded company commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 7 (1147) he was additionally granted command over personal company units.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，除同知歸德尹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he was appointed Vice Administrator of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 3 (1151) he was appointed vice administrator of Guide.

sentences.zh: 正隆初，為唐古部族節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenglong he became Military Commissioner of the Tangut Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenglong era he became military commissioner of the Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，為保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he became Military Commissioner of the Baoda Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 (1162) he became military commissioner of the Baoda Army.

sentences.zh: 是歲改鎮通遠。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to garrison Tongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was reassigned to garrison Tongyuan.

sentences.zh: 是時，宋軍十萬餘入河、隴，據險要，攻郡邑。

translations.literal: At that time more than a hundred thousand Song troops entered the He-Long region, held strategic passes, and attacked prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time over a hundred thousand Song troops entered the He-Long region, seized strategic passes, and attacked prefectures and districts.

sentences.zh: 元帥左都監合喜奏益兵。

translations.literal: The marshal's left supervising commissioner Hexi memorialized requesting additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal's Left Supervising Commissioner Hexi memorialized for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 詔益兵七千，遣吾里補與彰化軍節度使宗室璋等七人偕往，以備任使。

translations.literal: An edict added seven thousand troops and dispatched Wulibu together with Military Commissioner of the Zhanghua Army, the imperial clansman Zhang, and six others to go together, to be available for assignment as needed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added seven thousand troops and sent Wulibu with Military Commissioner Zhang of the Zhanghua Army and six others, to be deployed as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 進階龍虎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to General-in-Chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general-in-chief of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒於軍中。

translations.literal: He died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp.

sentences.zh: 蕭恭，字敬之，乃烈奚王之後也。

translations.literal: Xiao Gong, courtesy name Jingzhi, was a descendant of Prince Lie of the Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Gong, styled Jingzhi, was descended from Prince Lie of the Xi.

sentences.zh: 父翊，天輔間歸朝，從攻興中，遂以為興中尹。

translations.literal: His father Yi, during Tianfu submitted to the court, followed in the attack on Xingzhong, and was thereupon made Administrator of Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi submitted during the Tianfu era, took part in the attack on Xingzhong, and was appointed administrator of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 師還，以恭為質子。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Gong was left as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, Gong was left at court as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 宗望伐宋，翊當領建、興、成、川、懿五州兵為萬戶，軍帥以恭材勇，使代其父行，時年二十三。

translations.literal: When Zongwang campaigned against Song, Yi was to lead the troops of the five prefectures Jian, Xing, Cheng, Chuan, and Yi as a ten-thousand-household commander; the army commander, because Gong was talented and brave, had him go in his father's place; he was then twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang invaded Song, Yi was to command the forces of five prefectures as a ten-thousand-household commander; the commander, seeing Gong's talent and courage, sent him in his father's stead—he was only twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 至中山，宋兵出戰，恭先以所部擊敗之。

translations.literal: At Zhongshan, Song troops came out to fight; Gong first with his own command defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongshan the Song army came out to fight; Gong led his command in a preemptive strike and routed them.

sentences.zh: 經山東，及渡淮，襲康王，皆在軍中。

translations.literal: Passing through Shandong, crossing the Huai, and raiding Prince Kang—all were in the army with him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched through Shandong, crossed the Huai, and took part in the raid on Prince Kang—all as a member of the army.

sentences.zh: 師還，帥府承制授德州防禦使，奚人之屯濱、棣間者皆隸焉。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the marshal's headquarters, acting under authority, appointed him Defender of Dezhou, and the Xi people encamped between Bin and Di were all placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign, headquarters appointed him defender of Dezhou, with all Xi settlements between Bin and Di placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 改棣州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Defender of Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to defender of Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 皇統間，改同知橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: During Huangtong he was changed to Vice Commissioner of the Henghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangtong era he became vice commissioner of the Henghai Army.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複為太原少尹。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning, then was recalled from mourning to serve as Junior Administrator of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was recalled to serve as junior administrator of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 用廉，遷同知中京留守事。

translations.literal: For integrity he was transferred to Vice Military Commissioner of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for integrity, he was promoted to vice military commissioner of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部侍郎，授世襲謀克。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of War and granted a hereditary company command.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of war and was granted a hereditary company command.

sentences.zh: 坐問禁中起居狀，決杖，奪一官。

translations.literal: He was punished for inquiring about daily conduct records within the forbidden precincts, was sentenced to the rod, and stripped of one rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was flogged and demoted one rank for inquiring about daily conduct records within the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，為同知大興尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he became Vice Administrator of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 he became vice administrator of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷兵部尚書，為宋國生日使。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he was transferred to Minister of War and served as envoy for the Song emperor's birthday.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to minister of war and sent as envoy for the Song emperor's birthday.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去官，起複為侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's death, then was recalled from mourning to serve as Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard's Cavalry and Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother, then was recalled as commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 正隆四年，遷光祿大夫，複為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenglong he was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and again became Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 4 he was promoted to grand master of splendid happiness and again appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 是歲，經畫夏國邊界，還過臨潼，失所佩金牌。

translations.literal: That year, while surveying the Xia border, on his return he passed Lintong and lost the gold tablet he wore.
translations.idiomatic: That year, while demarcating the Xia border, he lost the gold tablet he wore when passing through Lintong on his return.

sentences.zh: 至太原，憂恚成疾。

translations.literal: When he reached Taiyuan, grief and distress turned into illness.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Taiyuan, grief and distress had made him ill.

sentences.zh: 時已具其事驛聞於朝，海陵複命給之，仍遣諭恭曰：「汝失信牌，亦猶不謹。

translations.literal: The matter had already been reported to court by courier; Hailing again ordered that it be given to him anew and still sent word to instruct Gong, saying: "You lost the credential tablet—this too shows lack of care.
translations.idiomatic: The matter had already been reported to court by courier; Hailing ordered a replacement issued and sent word to Gong: "You lost your credential tablet—that too shows carelessness.

sentences.zh: 朕方俟汝，欲有委使，乃稱疾耶？

translations.literal: I was just waiting for you, intending to assign you duties—yet you claim illness?
translations.idiomatic: I was waiting for you with assignments in mind—yet you claim to be ill?

sentences.zh: 必以去日身佩信牌，歸則無以為辭，欲朕先知耳。」

translations.literal: Surely because on the day you departed you wore the credential tablet on your person, and on return had no excuse, you wished me to know beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: Surely you wore the tablet when you left and had no excuse on return—you wanted me to know in advance."

sentences.zh: 使至，恭已疾篤，稽顙受命，俄頃而卒。

translations.literal: When the messenger arrived, Gong was already gravely ill; he bowed his forehead to the ground to receive the command, and in a moment died.
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger arrived, Gong was gravely ill; he kowtowed to receive the imperial message and died moments later.

sentences.zh: 海陵方遣使與其子護衛九哥馳視，乃戒府官使善護之。

translations.literal: Hailing had just dispatched a messenger with his son, the guardsman Jiuge, to hurry and see him, and had instructed the prefectural officials to care for him well.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had just sent his son Jiuge of the guards with a messenger to hurry to his side, instructing local officials to care for him well.

sentences.zh: 至保州，已聞訃矣，海陵深悼惜之。

translations.literal: When they reached Baozhou they had already heard the death announcement; Hailing deeply mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: At Baozhou they learned he had already died; Hailing mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 命九哥護喪以還，所過州府設奠。

translations.literal: He ordered Jiuge to escort the coffin back, and at every prefecture and district they passed through, offerings were set out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jiuge to escort the coffin home, with memorial offerings at every prefecture along the route.

sentences.zh: 喪至都，命百官致祭。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached the capital, he ordered all officials to offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached the capital, he ordered all officials to perform rites of mourning.

sentences.zh: 親臨奠，賻贈甚厚，並賜廄馬一。

translations.literal: He personally came to offer sacrifices; the funeral gifts were very generous, and he also bestowed one stable horse.
translations.idiomatic: He came in person to mourn; the funeral gifts were lavish, and he also bestowed a stable horse.

sentences.zh: 謂九哥曰：「爾父銜命，卒於道途，甚可悼惜。

translations.literal: He said to Jiuge: "Your father bore an imperial commission and died on the road—how deeply lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: He told Jiuge: "Your father died on the road while carrying out an imperial commission—how lamentable.

sentences.zh: 朕乘此馬十年，今賜汝父，可常控至柩前。

translations.literal: I have ridden this horse for ten years; now I bestow it on your father—you may lead it constantly before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: I have ridden this horse for ten years; I now give it to your father—lead it before the coffin throughout the journey.

sentences.zh: 既葬，汝則乘之。」

translations.literal: After the burial, you may ride it."
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, you may ride it yourself."

sentences.zh: 完顏習不主

translations.literal: Wanyan Xibuzhu
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Xibuzhu

sentences.zh: 完顏習不主，年十六，從伐宋，攻下懷仁縣，功居最。

translations.literal: Wanyan Xibuzhu, at age sixteen, followed in the campaign against Song, captured Huairen County, and his merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen, Wanyan Xibuzhu joined the campaign against Song, captured Huairen County, and ranked first in merit.

sentences.zh: 從睿宗經略陝西，以兵七百人入丹州諸山，遇盜三千，擊敗之。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Rui in operations in Shaanxi, entered the mountains of Danzhou with seven hundred troops, encountered three thousand bandits, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Rui in operations in Shaanxi, led seven hundred men into the mountains of Danzhou, met three thousand bandits, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又破賊四千，生擒其將帥。

translations.literal: He again defeated four thousand bandits and captured their generals alive.
translations.idiomatic: He again routed four thousand rebels and took their commanders alive.

sentences.zh: 出隴州，以兵四百敗敵數千。

translations.literal: Leaving Longzhou, with four hundred troops he defeated several thousand enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Longzhou, he routed several thousand enemy with four hundred men.

sentences.zh: 宋兵七千來取鞏州，複擊走之。

translations.literal: Seven thousand Song troops came to take Gongzhou; he again attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When seven thousand Song troops came to take Gongzhou, he drove them off again.

sentences.zh: 又以五千兵敗吳玠之眾三萬，白塔口遇敵五千，複敗之。

translations.literal: Again with five thousand troops he defeated Wu Jie's host of thirty thousand; at Baitakou he encountered five thousand enemy and again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: With five thousand men he routed Wu Jie's army of thirty thousand; at Baitakou he met five thousand enemy and defeated them as well.

sentences.zh: 別降定遠等寨。

translations.literal: Separately he induced Dingyuan and other stockades to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He also induced Dingyuan and other stockades to surrender.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，授同知臨洮尹，以憂去官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he was appointed Vice Administrator of Lintao and left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 2 he was appointed vice administrator of Lintao but left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 未期，以舊職起複，改孟州防禦使，遷臨洮尹。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period had ended he was recalled from mourning to his former post, was changed to Defender of Mengzhou, and transferred to Administrator of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning period ended he was recalled, appointed defender of Mengzhou, then administrator of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 複以罪罷。

translations.literal: Again he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 正隆三年，起為京兆尹，改河南尹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenglong he was recalled to serve as Administrator of Jingzhao and changed to Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 3 he was recalled as administrator of Jingzhao, then transferred to administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈胡剌

translations.literal: Geshilie Hula
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Hula

sentences.zh: 紇石烈胡剌，晦發川唵敦河人，徙西北路。

translations.literal: Geshilie Hula was a man of Endunhe on the Huifa River and was relocated to the Northwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Hula was from Endunhe on the Huifa River; his family was relocated to the Northwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 識契丹字，為帥府小吏。

translations.literal: He knew Khitan script and served as a petty clerk in the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Khitan script, he served as a clerk at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 梁王宗弼複陝西，久不通問。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Zongbi recovered Shaanxi, but for a long time there had been no communication.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Liang Zongbi recovered Shaanxi, communications had long been cut off.

sentences.zh: 睿宗在燕京，遣胡剌往候之。

translations.literal: Prince Rui was in Yanjing and dispatched Hula to go inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui, then at Yanjing, sent Hula to make contact.

sentences.zh: 是時，宗弼自鳳翔攻和尚原，使胡剌視彼中地形，修道築城。

translations.literal: At that time Zongbi from Fengxiang attacked Heshangyuan and had Hula survey the terrain there, repair roads, and build fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi was then attacking Heshangyuan from Fengxiang and sent Hula to survey the terrain, repair roads, and build fortifications.

sentences.zh: 天會十二年，往濱州密訪南邊事體，及觀劉豫治齊狀，盡得其虛實。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianhui he went to Binzhou to make secret inquiries into conditions on the southern frontier and to observe how Liu Yu governed Qi, learning the enemy's full situation.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 12 he went secretly to Binzhou to investigate southern conditions and observe Liu Yu's governance of Qi, learning the enemy's full dispositions.

sentences.zh: 睿宗甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Prince Rui greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui commended him highly.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，從宗弼渡淮，及下廬、和二州，大破張浚、韓世忠等軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong he followed Zongbi in crossing the Huai and in the reduction of Lu and He prefectures, inflicting a great defeat on the armies of Zhang Jun, Han Shizhong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong he followed Zongbi across the Huai and in the capture of Lu and He prefectures, crushing the armies of Zhang Jun, Han Shizhong, and others.

sentences.zh: 遣胡剌馳奏，賞以金盂、重彩五端、絹五匹。

translations.literal: He dispatched Hula to report by rapid courier and rewarded him with a gold bowl, five bolts of heavy-colored silk, and five bolts of plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hula with an urgent report and rewarded him with a gold bowl, five bolts of heavy silk, and five bolts of plain silk.

sentences.zh: 七年，授同知景州軍州事，以廉，加忠武校尉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Vice Administrator of Jingzhou's military and civil affairs; for integrity he was given the additional rank of Loyal and Martial Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed vice administrator of Jingzhou; for integrity he was also granted the rank of loyal and martial commandant.

sentences.zh: 天德初，以監察禦史分司行台，曆同知濟州防禦使事，入為監察禦史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he served as investigating censor on detached duty at the branch secretariat, passed through as Vice Administrator of Jizhou's defense affairs, and entered the capital as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiande he served as investigating censor at the branch secretariat, then as vice administrator of Jizhou, and finally entered the capital as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 秩滿再任。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was appointed to a second term.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was reappointed.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，遷刑部員外郎，與御史大夫白彥敬往西北部族市馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice and, with Censor-in-Chief Bai Yanjing, went to the tribal peoples of the northwest to purchase horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Justice and, with Censor-in-Chief Bai Yanjing, went to the northwestern tribes to purchase horses.

sentences.zh: 累轉泗州防禦使，三遷蒲與路節度使，移甯昌軍，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Defender of Sizhou, was thrice transferred to Military Commissioner of the Puyu Circuit, moved to the Ningchang Army, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as defender of Sizhou, was thrice transferred as military commissioner of the Puyu Circuit, moved to the Ningchang Army, and died there.

sentences.zh: 耶律恕

translations.literal: Yelü Shu
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Shu

sentences.zh: 耶律恕，字忠厚，本名耨里，遼橫帳秦王之族也。

translations.literal: Yelü Shu, courtesy name Zhonghou, original name Nouri, was of the clan of the Liao Horizontal-Account Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Shu, styled Zhonghou, born Nouri, belonged to the clan of the Liao Prince of Qin of the horizontal account.

sentences.zh: 為人謹願有志，喜讀書，通契丹大小字。

translations.literal: As a man he was cautious, sincere, and purposeful; he delighted in reading books and was versed in both the large and small Khitan scripts.
translations.idiomatic: Cautious, sincere, and purposeful, he loved learning and was versed in both forms of Khitan script.

sentences.zh: 與耶律高八來歸。

translations.literal: He came to submit together with Yelü Gaoba.
translations.idiomatic: He came over to the Jin together with Yelü Gaoba.

sentences.zh: 婁室問高八曰：「與爾同來者，誰可任用治軍旅事？」

translations.literal: Loushi asked Gaoba: "Of those who came with you, who can be employed to manage military affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Loushi asked Gaoba: "Of those who came with you, who is fit to manage military affairs?"

sentences.zh: 高八封曰：「耨里可。」

translations.literal: Gaoba replied in sealed memorial: "Nouri will do."
translations.idiomatic: Gaoba replied: "Nouri will do."

sentences.zh: 婁室與宗翰伐宋，恕隸前鋒，取和尚原，攻仙人關，特為睿宗所知，再除太原、真定少尹。

translations.literal: When Loushi and Zonghan campaigned against Song, Shu served under the vanguard, took Heshangyuan, attacked Xianrenguan, and was especially noticed by Prince Rui; he was twice appointed Junior Administrator of Taiyuan and Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: When Loushi and Zonghan invaded Song, Shu served in the vanguard, took Heshangyuan and attacked Xianrenguan, and won special notice from Prince Rui; he was twice appointed junior administrator of Taiyuan and Zhending.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝辟署陝西參謀，委以軍務，遷行台兵部侍郎，再遷尚書左司郎中。

translations.literal: Salihai recruited him to his staff as staff officer for Shaanxi, entrusted him with military affairs, transferred him to Vice Minister of War on the branch secretariat, and again transferred him to Director of the Left Department of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Salihai recruited him as staff officer for Shaanxi and entrusted him with military affairs; he rose to vice minister of war on the branch secretariat, then director of the left department.

sentences.zh: 海陵為平章政事，謂恕曰：「君亦有黨乎？」

translations.literal: When Hailing was Grand Councilor of the Secretariat, he said to Shu: "Do you too have a faction?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was grand councilor, he asked Shu: "Do you too have a faction?"

sentences.zh: 恕正色曰：「窮則獨善其身，達則兼善天下。

translations.literal: Shu said with a stern countenance: "In adversity one cultivates oneself alone; in success one cultivates the whole world.
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied gravely: "In adversity one cultivates oneself; in success one cultivates the whole world.

sentences.zh: 不以其道得之，非恕之志也，何朋黨之有！」

translations.literal: To obtain it by means not in accord with the Way is not Shu's aspiration—what factions could there be!"
translations.idiomatic: To obtain office by improper means is not my aim—what factions could I have!"

sentences.zh: 海陵徐曰：「前言戲之耳。」

translations.literal: Hailing said slowly: "What I said before was only in jest."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said slowly: "I was only jesting before."

sentences.zh: 久之，為沁南軍節度使，遷行台工部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long while he became Military Commissioner of the Qinnan Army and was transferred to Minister of Works on the branch secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became military commissioner of the Qinnan Army, then minister of works on the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 行台罷，改安國軍節度使，為參知政事。

translations.literal: When the branch secretariat was abolished, he was changed to Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army and made Associate Administrator of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the branch secretariat was abolished, he became military commissioner of the Anguo Army and associate administrator of affairs.

sentences.zh: 以疾求解，為興中尹，入為太子少保。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested release from office, became Administrator of Xingzhong, and entered the capital as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness he resigned, became administrator of Xingzhong, then entered the capital as junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 正隆元年致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenglong he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in the first year of Zhenglong.

sentences.zh: 封廣平郡王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 薨，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died; he was sixty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 二年，例贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year, by precedent he was posthumously granted Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was posthumously granted silver-glitter grand master of splendid happiness by precedent.

sentences.zh: 郭企忠

translations.literal: Guo Qizhong
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qizhong

sentences.zh: 郭企忠，字元弼，唐汾陽王子儀之後。

translations.literal: Guo Qizhong, courtesy name Yuanbi, was a descendant of Guo Ziyi, Prince of Fenyang of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qizhong, styled Yuanbi, was a descendant of Tang's Prince of Fenyang, Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 郭氏自子儀至承勳，皆節鎮北方。

translations.literal: The Guo clan from Ziyi to Chengxun all held military governorships in the north.
translations.idiomatic: From Ziyi to Chengxun, the Guo clan had held military commands in the north for generations.

sentences.zh: 唐季，承勳入於遼，子孫繼為天德軍節度使，至昌金降為副使。

translations.literal: In the late Tang, Chengxun entered Liao; his descendants in succession became Military Commissioners of the Tiande Army, down to Changjin, who was demoted to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In late Tang, Chengxun entered Liao service; his descendants served as military commissioners of the Tiande Army until Changjin was reduced to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 企忠幼孤，事母孝謹。

translations.literal: Qizhong was orphaned young and served his mother with filial care and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Qizhong served his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十三，居母喪，哀毀如成人。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, during his mother's mourning, his grief and emaciation were like those of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, mourning his mother, his grief was as deep as a grown man's.

sentences.zh: 服除，襲父官，加左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he inherited his father's post and was given the additional title of Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited his father's post and was given the additional title of left regular attendant of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天輔中，大軍至雲中，遣耶律坦招撫諸部。

translations.literal: During Tianfu the main army reached Yunzhong and dispatched Yelü Tan to win over and pacify the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, when the main army reached Yunzhong, Yelü Tan was sent to win over the various tribes.

sentences.zh: 企忠來降。

translations.literal: Qizhong came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhong submitted.

sentences.zh: 軍帥命同勾當天德軍節度使事，徙所部居於韓州。

translations.literal: The army commander ordered him to jointly manage the affairs of the Tiande Army military commissioner and moved his command to settle at Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The commander appointed him to assist in the affairs of the Tiande Army and relocated his command to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及見太祖，問知其家世，禮遇優厚，以白鷹賜之。

translations.literal: When he met the Taizu Emperor and inquired into his family background, he was treated with exceptional courtesy and bestowed a white hawk.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Emperor Taizu and learned his lineage, he was treated with exceptional honor and given a white hawk.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，伐宋，領西南諸部番、漢軍兵，為猛安，從破雁門，屯兵，加桂州管內觀察留後，鎮代州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui, campaigning against Song, he led the tribal and Han troops of the various southwestern tribes as a meng'an, followed in the capture of Yanmen, garrisoned troops, was given the additional title of Military Governor and Observer within Guizhou's jurisdiction, and garrisoned Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 3, campaigning against Song, he led southwestern tribal and Han forces as a meng'an commander, helped capture Yanmen, and was appointed military governor and observer of Guizhou while garrisoning Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊楊麻胡等聚眾數千於五台，企忠與同知州事迪里討平之。

translations.literal: The next year the bandits Yang Mahu and others gathered several thousand men on Wutai; Qizhong together with Vice Administrator of the prefecture Diri suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yang Mahu and others gathered several thousand rebels on Wutai; Qizhong and Vice Administrator Diri suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 遷知汾州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Fenzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administer Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時汾州初下，居民多為軍士掠去，城邑蕭然。

translations.literal: At that time Fenzhou had just been taken; many residents had been carried off by soldiers, and the city was desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhou had just fallen; soldiers had carried off many residents, and the city lay desolate.

sentences.zh: 企忠詣帥府力請，願聽其親舊贖還。

translations.literal: Qizhong went to headquarters and urgently petitioned, wishing to allow their kin and friends to ransom them back.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhong urgently petitioned headquarters to allow families and friends to ransom them back.

sentences.zh: 帥府從之。

translations.literal: Headquarters consented.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，完實如故。

translations.literal: Before long, the population was complete as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the population was restored.

sentences.zh: 石州賊閻先生眾數萬至城下，僚屬慮有內變，請為備。

translations.literal: The bandit Master Yan of Shizhou with a host of tens of thousands came to the city walls; the subordinates feared internal revolt and requested preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Master Yan of Shizhou led tens of thousands to the walls; his staff feared treachery within and urged precautions.

sentences.zh: 企忠曰：「吾於汾人有德，保無他。」

translations.literal: Qizhong said: "I have shown virtue toward the people of Fen—assuredly there will be no other trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Qizhong said: "I have treated the people of Fen well—there will be no trouble within."

sentences.zh: 乃率吏民城守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led officials and people in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then led officials and citizens in the defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 會援至，合擊，破之。

translations.literal: When reinforcements arrived, they joined in the attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When reinforcements arrived, they joined forces and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 六年，改靜江軍節度留後，遷天德軍節度使、汴京步軍都指揮使，累遷金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to Military Governor and Acting Commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, transferred to Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Bianjing Infantry, and was promoted in succession to General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became acting commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, then military commissioner of the Tiande Army and commander of Bianjing infantry, rising to general-in-chief of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，權沁州刺史。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was acting Prefect of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he served as acting prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 到官歲餘，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year in office he died at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year in office he died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 烏孫訛論

translations.literal: Wusun Elun
translations.idiomatic: Wusun Elun

sentences.zh: 烏孫訛論，善騎射，襲父撒改謀克，從蒙刮攻東京及廣寧，擊北京山賊，皆有功。

translations.literal: Wusun Elun was skilled in horsemanship and archery, inherited his father Sagai's company command, followed Menggua in attacking the Eastern Capital and Guangning, and struck the bandits of the Northern Capital mountains—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, Wusun Elun inherited his father Sagai's company command, followed Menggua in attacks on the Eastern Capital and Guangning, and fought bandits in the northern mountains—all with distinction.

sentences.zh: 蕭霸哲來攻恩州，訛論以六十騎偵之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Bazhe came to attack Enzhou, Elun reconnoitered with sixty horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Bazhe attacked Enzhou, Elun scouted with sixty horsemen.

sentences.zh: 逮夜，遇敵數百騎，掩擊之，生獲三人，知霸哲眾九萬且至，故蒙刮得以為備，遂破霸哲。

translations.literal: By night he encountered several hundred enemy horsemen, made a surprise attack, captured three alive, and learned that Bazhe's host of ninety thousand was about to arrive; thus Menggua was able to prepare defenses and thereupon defeated Bazhe.
translations.idiomatic: By night he surprised several hundred enemy horsemen, took three prisoners, and learned that Bazhe's army of ninety thousand was approaching—allowing Menggua to prepare and defeat him.

sentences.zh: 宗望伐宋，已至汴，訛論破尉氏、中牟援兵，取其城。

translations.literal: When Zongwang campaigned against Song and had already reached Bian, Elun defeated the relief troops of Weishi and Zhongmou and took their cities.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang reached Bian during the Song campaign, Elun defeated relief forces at Weishi and Zhongmou and captured those cities.

sentences.zh: 久之，以兵百五十人破敵一千於滄州西。

translations.literal: After a long while, with one hundred fifty troops he defeated a thousand enemy west of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with a hundred and fifty men he routed a thousand enemy west of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，再伐宋。

translations.literal: The next year they campaigned against Song again.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the army invaded Song again.

sentences.zh: 蒙刮戍開州，訛論以騎四百守河，複敗千餘人，斬首七百餘。

translations.literal: Menggua garrisoned Kaizhou; Elun with four hundred cavalry guarded the river, again defeated more than a thousand men, and beheaded more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: While Menggua garrisoned Kaizhou, Elun held the river with four hundred cavalry, routed over a thousand enemy, and took more than seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 宗弼渡淮，阿里先具舟于江上，聞王善兵扼其前。

translations.literal: Zongbi crossed the Huai; Ali had first prepared boats on the river and heard that Wang Shan's troops blocked the way ahead.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi crossed the Huai, Ali had prepared boats on the river but learned that Wang Shan's army blocked the way ahead.

sentences.zh: 宗弼使訛論濟師敗王善於和州北。

translations.literal: Zongbi had Elun ferry troops across and defeat Wang Shan north of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi sent Elun with reinforcements to defeat Wang Shan north of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 李成以兵七萬據烏江，訛論帥二千人直前敗之。

translations.literal: Li Cheng with seventy thousand troops held Wujiang; Elun led two thousand men straight forward and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng held Wujiang with seventy thousand men; Elun led two thousand in a frontal assault and routed him.

sentences.zh: 宗弼遂渡江至江寧。

translations.literal: Zongbi thereupon crossed the river and reached Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi then crossed the Yangzi and reached Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十五年，沂州竇防禦叛。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Defender of Yizhou, Dou, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the defender of Yizhou, Dou, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 訛論敗之，獲竇防禦。

translations.literal: Elun defeated him and captured Defender Dou.
translations.idiomatic: Elun defeated him and captured Dou.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，授猛安，加昭武大將軍。

translations.literal: Recording his past and present merit, they appointed him meng'an and gave him the additional rank of Illustrious Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated service he was appointed meng'an commander and granted the rank of illustrious martial general.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再取河南，訛論以五十騎敗楊家賊五百於徐州東。

translations.literal: When Zongbi again took Henan, Elun with fifty horsemen defeated five hundred Yang-family bandits east of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi recovered Henan again, Elun with fifty horsemen routed five hundred Yang-family rebels east of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以功受賞，不可勝計。

translations.literal: For his merit he received rewards beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: His rewards for merit were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，除唐州刺史，移淄州，遷石壘部族節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was appointed Prefect of Tangzhou, transferred to Zizhou, and promoted to Military Commissioner of the Shilei Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2 he was appointed prefect of Tangzhou, transferred to Zizhou, then promoted to military commissioner of the Shilei tribes.

sentences.zh: 行至北京，病卒。

translations.literal: When he reached the Northern Capital he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness en route at the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 顏盞門都

translations.literal: Yanzhan Mendu
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhan Mendu

sentences.zh: 顏盞門都，隆州帕里幹山人也。

translations.literal: Yanzhan Mendu was a man of Paliganshan in Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhan Mendu was a native of Paliganshan in Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 身長，美須髯。

translations.literal: He was tall, with handsome beard and whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and handsome, with a fine beard.

sentences.zh: 天會間，從其兄羊艾在軍中。

translations.literal: During Tianhui he followed his elder brother Yang'ai in the army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhui era he served in the army with his elder brother Yang'ai.

sentences.zh: 方取汴京，其兄戰歿，遂擐甲代其兄充軍。

translations.literal: Just as Bianjing was being taken, his brother died in battle; he thereupon donned armor and took his brother's place in the army.
translations.idiomatic: During the capture of Bianjing his brother was killed in battle; Mendu donned armor and took his place in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 睿宗定陝右，以門都為蒲輦，隸監軍杲親管萬戶，攻饒風關。

translations.literal: When Prince Rui pacified western Shaanxi, Mendu was made a puyan and placed under the personally commanded ten-thousand-household unit of Supervising General Gao, attacking Raofeng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Rui pacified western Shaanxi, Mendu served as puyan under Supervising General Gao's personal command and attacked Raofeng Pass.

sentences.zh: 至坊州，杲欲與總管蒲魯虎會於鳳翔，遣門都領六十騎先往期會。

translations.literal: At Fangzhou, Gao wished to meet Commissioner Puluhu at Fengxiang and dispatched Mendu to lead sixty horsemen ahead to keep the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At Fangzhou, Gao planned to meet Commissioner Puluhu at Fengxiang and sent Mendu ahead with sixty horsemen.

sentences.zh: 及還，備得地形險厄，賞銀五十兩。

translations.literal: On his return he had fully learned the dangerous terrain and was rewarded with fifty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he had mapped the difficult terrain and was rewarded with fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 其後樑王宗弼駐軍山東，遣人詣陝西，特召門都至。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince of Liang Zongbi was stationed in Shandong; he sent someone to Shaanxi especially to summon Mendu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince of Liang Zongbi was stationed in Shandong, he specially summoned Mendu from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 令齎廢齊及安撫百姓詔書，往諭監軍宗室杲。

translations.literal: He ordered him to carry the edicts abolishing Qi and pacifying the people and go to instruct Supervising General Gao of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent with edicts abolishing Qi and pacifying the populace to convey them to Supervising General Gao.

sentences.zh: 門都既還，宗弼賞以良馬銀絹。

translations.literal: When Mendu had returned, Zongbi rewarded him with fine horses, silver, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Mendu returned, Zongbi rewarded him with fine horses, silver, and silk.

sentences.zh: 事畢，複遣從杲。

translations.literal: When the matter was finished, he was again sent to follow Gao.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission was done, he was sent back to serve under Gao.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，叛將定國軍節度使李世輔偽邀杲至私署，以獻甲為名，遂以兵劫執而去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan the rebel Military Commissioner of the Dingguo Army, Li Shifu, falsely invited Gao to his private office on the pretext of presenting armor, then seized him by force of arms and carried him off.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjuan the rebel military commissioner Li Shifu lured Gao to his private office on the pretext of presenting armor, then seized him by force.

sentences.zh: 門都突出，以告押軍猛安完顏撻懶，同率兵追及，首出與戰，杲由此得脫，以功遷明威將軍。

translations.literal: Mendu broke out, reported to the army escort meng'an Wanyan Talan, and together led troops in pursuit; he was first out to fight, and Gao thereby escaped; for this merit he was transferred to Illustrious Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: Mendu escaped, alerted Meng'an Wanyan Talan, and together they pursued; Mendu led the charge and Gao escaped—for this he was promoted to illustrious martial general.

sentences.zh: 複從杲招複陝西，進至鳳翔。

translations.literal: Again he followed Gao in winning back Shaanxi and advanced to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Gao in recovering Shaanxi and advanced to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 齊國初廢，諸路多反復不一。

translations.literal: When Qi was first abolished, the various circuits were mostly unstable and inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was abolished, the circuits were in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 杲授門都牌劄，令往撫定。

translations.literal: Gao gave Mendu written credentials and ordered him to go pacify and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao gave Mendu written authority and sent him to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 門都所至，多張甲兵，從者安之，違者討之，帖然無複叛者，杲甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Wherever Mendu went he displayed many armored troops; those who followed were reassured, those who defied were punished, and all were submissive with no further rebels; Gao greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Mendu went he displayed armed force; the compliant were reassured, the defiant punished—and rebellion ceased; Gao praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，遷廣威將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong he was transferred to Broad Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong he was promoted to broad martial general.

sentences.zh: 四年，授同知通遠軍節度使事，改知保安軍事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Tongyuan Army and changed to administer Bao'an military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became vice commissioner of the Tongyuan Army, then administrator of Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，為丹州刺史兼知軍事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he became Prefect of Danzhou and concurrently administered military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 3 he became prefect of Danzhou with concurrent military command.

sentences.zh: 正隆初，為甯州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenglong he became Prefect of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenglong he became prefect of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 大定初，宋將吳璘等以軍數十萬人據秦、隴，元帥府承制以門都為勇烈軍都總管，領軍討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading the Song generals Wu Lin and others with an army of several hundred thousand held Qin and Long; the marshal's headquarters, acting under authority, made Mendu Commander-in-Chief of the Yonglie Army and had him lead troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading the Song generals Wu Lin and others held Qin and Long with hundreds of thousands of troops; headquarters appointed Mendu commander of the Yonglie Army to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 宋人保據德順。

translations.literal: The Song held and defended Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Song held Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 都監合喜遣武威軍副都總管夾谷查剌，會宗室璋，議征討之策。

translations.literal: Supervising Commissioner Hexi dispatched Deputy Commander-in-Chief Jiagu Zhala of the Wuwei Army to meet the imperial clansman Zhang and discuss strategies for campaign and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Commissioner Hexi sent Deputy Commander Jiagu Zhala of the Wuwei Army to confer with Zhang of the imperial clan on strategy.

sentences.zh: 璋及閘都曰：「須都監親至，敵必退矣。」

translations.literal: Zhang and Mendu said: "The supervising commissioner must come in person, and the enemy will surely retreat."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Mendu said: "The supervising commissioner must come in person—the enemy will surely retreat."

sentences.zh: 合喜領軍四萬來赴，遂複德順州。

translations.literal: Hexi led forty thousand troops to come to their aid, and thereupon recovered Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi arrived with forty thousand troops and recovered Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，秦、隴平，以功遷金吾衛上將軍，授通遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: The next year Qin and Long were pacified; for his merit he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Golden Crow Guard and appointed Military Commissioner of the Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Qin and Long were pacified; for his service he was promoted to general-in-chief of the Golden Crow Guard and appointed military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 五年，改慶陽尹，兼本路兵馬都總管，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Administrator of Qingyang and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of Troops and Horses of that circuit; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became administrator of Qingyang and commander of that circuit's forces; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 十九年，錄功，以子六哥世襲本路曷懶兀主猛安敵骨論窟申謀克，授武功將軍。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year his merit was recorded; his son Liuge was granted hereditary succession to the yilan wuzhu meng'an digulun kushin company command on this circuit and appointed General of Martial Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year his son Liuge was granted hereditary succession to the digulun kushin company command on this circuit and appointed general of martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 門都性忠厚謹愨，安置營壁，尤能慎密。

translations.literal: Mendu's nature was loyal, generous, cautious, and sincere; in arranging camps and stockades he was especially careful and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, sincere, and cautious by nature, Mendu was especially meticulous in arranging camps and defenses.

sentences.zh: 有敵忽來，雖矢石至前，泰然自若，乃號令士卒如平時，由是人益安附，而功易成焉。

translations.literal: When the enemy suddenly came, though arrows and stones reached before him, he was calm and at ease, and gave orders to the soldiers as in ordinary times; thereby people were all the more reassured and attached, and achievements were easily accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy struck suddenly, though arrows and stones flew before him, he remained calm and commanded his men as in peacetime—winning their trust and making victory easier.

sentences.zh: 僕散渾坦

translations.literal: Pusan Huntan
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Huntan

sentences.zh: 僕散渾坦，蒲與路挾懣人也。

translations.literal: Pusan Huntan was a man of Jiamen on the Puyu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Huntan was a native of Jiamen on the Puyu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，勇健有力，善騎射。

translations.literal: He was seven feet tall, brave, strong, and powerful, and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Seven feet tall, brave and powerful, he excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 年十六，從其父胡沒速征伐。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he followed his father Humosu in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he joined his father Humosu on campaign.

sentences.zh: 初授修武校尉，為宗弼紮也。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Cultivated Martial Commandant and served as Zongbi's zhaye.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed cultivated martial commandant and served as Zongbi's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，與宋岳飛相拒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he opposed the Song general Yue Fei.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 2 he faced the Song general Yue Fei in battle.

sentences.zh: 渾坦領六十騎，深入覘伺，至鄢陵，敗宋護糧餉軍七百餘人，多所俘獲。

translations.literal: Huntan led sixty horsemen in deep reconnaissance; at Yanling he defeated more than seven hundred Song troops guarding grain supplies and took many captives.
translations.idiomatic: Huntan led sixty horsemen deep into enemy territory; at Yanling he routed over seven hundred Song troops guarding supplies and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 皇統九年，除慈州刺史，再遷利涉軍節度使，授世襲濟州和術海鸞猛安涉里斡設謀克。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Huangtong he was appointed Prefect of Cizhou, was again transferred to Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army, and granted hereditary succession to the jizhou heshuhailuan meng'an sheriganshe company command.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 9 he became prefect of Cizhou, then military commissioner of the Lishe Army, and was granted hereditary command of the sheriganshe company at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，以憂去官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 起復舊職，曆泰寧、永定軍，改咸平尹。

translations.literal: He was recalled from mourning to his former post, passed through the Taining and Yongding armies, and was changed to Administrator of Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to his former post, he served in the Taining and Yongding armies, then became administrator of Xianping.

sentences.zh: 海陵殺渾坦弟樞密使忽土，召渾坦至南京。

translations.literal: Hailing killed Huntan's younger brother, the Censor-in-Chief Hutu, and summoned Huntan to the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing executed Huntan's brother, Censor-in-Chief Hutu, he summoned Huntan to the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 既見，沈思久之，謂之曰：「汝有功舊，不因忽土得官，以此致罪，甚可矜憫。」

translations.literal: When he had seen him, after long reflection he said to him: "You are an old meritorious servant; you did not obtain office through Hutu, yet for this you have been implicated in guilt—how deeply pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: When they met, after long silence Hailing said: "You are an old servant with merit; you did not owe your office to Hutu, yet you have been implicated—how pitiable."

sentences.zh: 遂釋之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he released him.
translations.idiomatic: He then released him.

sentences.zh: 改興平軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Military Commissioner of the Xingping Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Xingping Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，以為廣甯尹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he was made Administrator of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was appointed administrator of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 窩斡反，為行軍都統，與曷懶路總管徒單克寧俱在左翼，敗窩斡於長濼。

translations.literal: When Wowo rebelled, he became campaign commander-in-chief; together with Commissioner of the Yilan Circuit Tushan Kening, both on the left wing, he defeated Wowo at Changpo.
translations.idiomatic: When Wowo rebelled, he served as campaign commander-in-chief; with Yilan Commissioner Tushan Kening on the left wing, he defeated Wowo at Changpo.

sentences.zh: 改臨潢尹。

translations.literal: He was changed to Administrator of Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 賊平，賜金帛。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was bestowed gold and silks.
