translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was suppressed, he was rewarded with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 改曷懶路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commander-in-Chief of Troops and Horses of the Yilan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became commander of the Yilan circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 徙顯德軍、慶陽尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Xiande Army and Administrator of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Xiande Army and then administrator of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 致仕。

translations.literal: He retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired.

sentences.zh: 大定十二年，上思舊功，起為利涉軍節度使，複以金紫光祿大夫致仕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dading the emperor recalled his old merit and recalled him to serve as Military Commissioner of the Lishe Army; again he retired as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purple Tassel.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 12 the emperor, remembering his old service, recalled him as military commissioner of the Lishe Army; he retired again as golden-purple grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 渾坦曆一十七官，未嘗為佐貳。

translations.literal: Huntan held seventeen offices in succession and never served as a deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Huntan held seventeen offices in succession and never served as a deputy.

sentences.zh: 性沈厚有識，雖未嘗學問，明於聽斷，所至有治聲雲。

translations.literal: His nature was deep, steady, and perceptive; though he had never studied, he was clear in hearing cases and rendering judgment, and wherever he went there was a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Deep, steady, and perceptive by nature, though unlettered he was skilled in judgment, and wherever he served he earned a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 鄭建充

translations.literal: Zheng Jianchong
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jianchong

sentences.zh: 鄭建充，字仲實，其先京兆人，占籍鄜州。

translations.literal: Zheng Jianchong, courtesy name Zhongshi, his ancestors were men of Jingzhao and were registered at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jianchong, styled Zhongshi, was descended from Jingzhao families registered at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 仕宋，累官知延安府事。

translations.literal: He served the Song and was promoted in succession to administer Yan'an Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Song and rose to administer Yan'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天會七年來降，仍知延安府，屯兵三千。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui he came to surrender and still administered Yan'an Prefecture, garrisoning three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 7 he submitted and continued to administer Yan'an with a garrison of three thousand.

sentences.zh: 宋劉光烈兵八萬來攻建充，相距四十餘日。

translations.literal: The Song general Liu Guanglie with eighty thousand troops came to attack Jianchong; they faced each other for more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Liu Guanglie attacked with eighty thousand men; the two sides faced each other for over forty days.

sentences.zh: 攻益急，建充遣人會斜喝軍，夾擊破之，俘其裨將賀貴。

translations.literal: The attack grew fiercer; Jianchong sent someone to join Xiehe's army in a pincer attack and defeated them, capturing their vice general He Gui.
translations.idiomatic: As the attack intensified, Jianchong coordinated with Xiehe's army in a pincer movement, routing the enemy and capturing Vice General He Gui.

sentences.zh: 遷節制司統制軍馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander of Troops and Horses under the Military Control Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of forces under the Military Control Office.

sentences.zh: 改京兆府路兵馬都監。

translations.literal: He was changed to Supervising Commander of Troops and Horses of the Jingzhao Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became supervising commander of the Jingzhao circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 敗宋曲端于彭原。

translations.literal: He defeated the Song general Qu Duan at Pengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Song general Qu Duan at Pengyuan.

sentences.zh: 高昌宗據延安，為宋守，建充擊之，盡複城邑。

translations.literal: Gao Changzong held Yan'an and defended it for the Song; Jianchong attacked him and fully recovered the cities and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Changzong held Yan'an for the Song; Jianchong attacked and recovered all the towns.

sentences.zh: 複知延安軍府事。

translations.literal: Again he administered the military and civil affairs of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He again administered Yan'an's military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，累遷博州團練使，知寧州。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, he was promoted in succession to Militia Commissioner of Bozhou and Administrator of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was established, he rose to militia commissioner of Bozhou and administrator of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，朝廷以地賜宋，為宋環慶路經略安撫副使，仍知寧州。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished, the court ceded the territory to Song; he became Vice Military Governor and Pacification Commissioner of the Song Huanqing Circuit and still administered Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was abolished and the territory returned to Song, he became vice military governor and pacification commissioner of the Huanqing circuit while still administering Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 天眷複取陝西，仍以為經略安撫使，知慶陽。

translations.literal: In Tianjuan they again took Shaanxi; he was again made Military Governor and Pacification Commissioner and administered Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianjuan brought Shaanxi back under Jin control, he was again appointed military governor and pacification commissioner at Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 從破甘穀城，改平涼尹。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Gangu City and was changed to Administrator of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Gangu and was appointed administrator of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 是時營建南京宮室，大發河東、陝西材木，浮河而下，經砥柱之險，筏工多沉溺，有司不敢以聞，乃誣以逃亡，錮其家。

translations.literal: At that time, constructing the palace halls of the Southern Capital, they conscripted timber on a great scale from Hedong and Shaanxi, floated it down the river, and passed the peril of Jizhi; many raft workers drowned, but the officials dared not report it and instead falsely charged them with flight, imprisoning their families.
translations.idiomatic: While building the Southern Capital palace, timber was conscripted from Hedong and Shaanxi and floated downriver past the perilous Jizhi rapids; many raft workers drowned, but officials dared not report it and instead charged their families with desertion.

sentences.zh: 建充白其事，請至砥柱解筏，順流散下，令善遊者下流接出之，而錮者得釋。

translations.literal: Jianchong reported the matter and requested that at Jizhi the rafts be dismantled and the timber sent downstream in scattered pieces, with skilled swimmers downstream to recover it—and those imprisoned were released.
translations.idiomatic: Jianchong reported the matter and proposed dismantling rafts at Jizhi, sending timber downstream in sections with skilled swimmers to recover it—and the imprisoned families were released.

sentences.zh: 正隆軍興，括筋角造軍器，百姓往往椎牛取之，或生拔取其角，牛有泣下者。

translations.literal: When Zhenglong raised armies, they requisitioned sinews and horns to make weapons; the common people often slaughtered cattle to obtain them, or pulled the horns off while the animals were alive, and some cattle wept tears.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenglong's military buildup, sinews and horns were requisitioned for weapons; commoners slaughtered cattle or pulled horns from living animals, and some cattle were seen to weep.

sentences.zh: 建充白其事於朝。

translations.literal: Jianchong reported the matter to court.
translations.idiomatic: Jianchong memorialized the court about this.

sentences.zh: 建充性剛暴，常畜猘犬十數，奴僕有罪既笞，已複嗾犬齧之，骨肉都盡。

translations.literal: Jianchong's nature was harsh and violent; he constantly kept a dozen or so fierce dogs; when slaves and servants had been flogged for an offense, he would again set the dogs on them to bite until flesh and bone were entirely consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh and violent by nature, Jianchong kept a dozen fierce dogs; after flogging a servant for an offense, he would set the dogs on him until nothing remained of flesh or bone.

sentences.zh: 雖謙遜下士，于敵己上一無所屈。

translations.literal: Though humble and deferential toward scholars, toward enemies and himself he yielded in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Though humble toward scholars, he yielded to no enemy and compromised with no one.

sentences.zh: 省部文移有不應法度，輒置之坐下，或即毀裂，由是在位者銜之。

translations.literal: When documents from the ministries did not conform to law, he would place them beneath his seat or immediately tear them up; thereby those in office harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: When ministry documents violated the law, he would set them aside or tear them up on the spot, earning the resentment of his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 軍胥李換竊用公帑，自度不得免，乃誣建充藏甲欲反，更再鞫，皆無狀。

translations.literal: The army clerk Li Huan embezzled public funds; judging that he could not escape punishment, he falsely accused Jianchong of hiding armor and plotting rebellion; after repeated interrogations, there was no evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Army clerk Li Huan embezzled public funds; fearing punishment, he falsely accused Jianchong of hoarding arms and plotting rebellion, but repeated investigations found no evidence.

sentences.zh: 方奏上，攝事者素與建充有隙，恐其得釋，使吏持文書紿建充曰：「朝省有命，奈何？」

translations.literal: Just as the memorial was being submitted, the acting official, who had long borne a grudge against Jianchong and feared he might be released, had a clerk bring documents and deceive Jianchong, saying: "The court has issued an order—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: As the memorial was being submitted, the acting official, who bore a grudge against Jianchong and feared his release, had a clerk deceive him with forged documents: "The court has issued an order—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 建充曰：「惟汝所為。」

translations.literal: Jianchong said: "Do as you will."
translations.idiomatic: Jianchong said: "Do as you will."

sentences.zh: 是夜，死於獄中。

translations.literal: That night he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: That night he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 長子訴亦死焉。

translations.literal: His eldest son Su also died there.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Su died as well.

sentences.zh: 烏古論三合

translations.literal: Wugulun Sanhe
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Sanhe

sentences.zh: 十八年，世宗追錄三合舊勞，授其子大興河北西路愛也窟河世襲猛安阿里門河謀克，階武功將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Emperor Shizong posthumously recorded Sanhe's old merit and appointed his son Daxing hereditary meng'an of Aiyekuhe on the Hebei West Circuit and company commander of Alimenhe, with the rank of General of Martial Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Emperor Shizong posthumously honored Sanhe's service and granted his son Daxing hereditary command of the Alimenhe company on the Hebei West Circuit, with the rank of general of martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 移剌溫

translations.literal: Yila Wen
translations.idiomatic: Yila Wen

sentences.zh: 移剌溫本名阿撒，遼橫帳人，工契丹小字。

translations.literal: Yila Wen's original name was Asa; he was a man of the Liao horizontal account and was skilled in the small Khitan script.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Wen, born Asa, was of the Liao horizontal account and skilled in the small Khitan script.

sentences.zh: 睿宗為左副元帥伐宋，溫從大抃渡江，辟江寧府都巡檢。

translations.literal: When Prince Rui was Left Vice Marshal campaigning against Song, Wen followed Dabian in crossing the river and was recruited as Chief Inspector of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Rui campaigned against Song as left vice marshal, Wen followed Dabian across the Yangzi and was appointed chief inspector of Jiangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 江甯、太平初下，宋遣諜人扇構百姓，應者數萬人。

translations.literal: When Jiangning and Taiping had just been taken, Song sent spies to incite the common people; tens of thousands responded.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning and Taiping had just fallen, Song agents incited the populace and tens of thousands responded.

sentences.zh: 溫擒其諜者，遂不敢竊發。

translations.literal: Wen captured their spies, and they no longer dared act in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Wen captured the spies, and the plot never materialized.

sentences.zh: 宗弼嘉之，賜銀千兩、重彩百端、絹二百匹。

translations.literal: Zongbi praised him and bestowed one thousand taels of silver, one hundred bolts of heavy-colored silk, and two hundred bolts of plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi commended him and rewarded him with a thousand taels of silver, a hundred bolts of heavy silk, and two hundred bolts of plain silk.

sentences.zh: 宗弼每出征伐，未嘗不在行間。

translations.literal: Whenever Zongbi went on campaign, Wen was never absent from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Wen accompanied Zongbi on every campaign.

sentences.zh: 除同知河北西路轉運使事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of Transport Affairs of the Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice transport commissioner of the Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會宗弼巡邊，溫從軍，不之官。

translations.literal: When Zongbi inspected the frontier, Wen followed the army and did not take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi inspected the frontier, Wen joined the army and did not report to his post.

sentences.zh: 宗弼入朝，熙宗宴群臣，宗弼欲有奏請，已被酒失次，溫掖而出宮。

translations.literal: When Zongbi entered court, Emperor Xizong feasted the ministers; Zongbi wished to make a memorial but, already drunk, lost proper decorum; Wen supported him and led him out of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At court Emperor Xizong feasted the ministers; Zongbi, already drunk, wished to address the throne but lost his composure; Wen supported him and escorted him from the palace.

sentences.zh: 明日，熙宗謂宗弼曰：「阿撒事叔甚謹，不可去左右。」

translations.literal: The next day Xizong said to Zongbi: "Asa serves his uncle with great care; he must not be kept from your side."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xizong told Zongbi: "Asa serves you with great devotion; keep him at your side."

sentences.zh: 由是宗弼益親信之。

translations.literal: Thereby Zongbi trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Zongbi trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂女婿紇石烈志寧曰：「汝可效阿撒之為人也，可以幾古人矣。」

translations.literal: He once said to his son-in-law Geshilie Zhining: "You may emulate Asa in conduct—you could nearly match the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: He once told his son-in-law Geshilie Zhining: "You should emulate Asa in conduct—you might nearly match the ancients."

sentences.zh: 未幾，除同知中京路都轉運使事，累遷左諫議大夫兼修起居注。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Metropolitan Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit, and was promoted in succession to Left Remonstrating Grandee and Compiler of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became vice metropolitan transport commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit, then rose to left remonstrating grandee and compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 正隆伐宋，以本官為濟州路行軍萬戶，從至揚州。

translations.literal: When Zhenglong campaigned against Song, with his existing office he served as Campaign Ten-Thousand-Household Commander of the Jizhou Circuit and followed to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenglong campaign against Song he served as campaign ten-thousand-household commander of the Jizhou Circuit and followed the army to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 軍還，除同知宣徽院事。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was appointed vice director of the palace domestic service.

sentences.zh: 世宗禦饌不適口，召溫嘗之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong found the imperial meal unpalatable, he summoned Wen to taste it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong found his meal unpalatable, he summoned Wen to taste it.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「味非不美也，蓋南北邊事未息，聖慮有所在耳。」

translations.literal: He reported: "The flavor is not unpleasing; it is rather that northern and southern frontier affairs have not yet ceased, and Your Majesty's thoughts are elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The flavor is not poor; Your Majesty's mind is on the unsettled northern and southern frontiers."

sentences.zh: 上意遂釋。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was thereupon relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mood lifted.

sentences.zh: 曆永定、震武、崇義節度使，移臨海軍。

translations.literal: He passed through the military commissioners of Yongding, Zhenwu, and Chongyi and was transferred to the Linhai Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military commissioner of Yongding, Zhenwu, and Chongyi, then transferred to the Linhai Army.

sentences.zh: 州治近水，秋雨，水潦暴至城下，城頗決，百姓惶駭，不知所為。

translations.literal: The prefectural seat was near water; in the autumn rains floodwaters suddenly rose to beneath the walls, the walls broke in many places, and the common people were terrified and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural seat lay near water; autumn rains brought sudden floods to the walls, which breached in places, and the people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 溫躬督役夫繕完之，雖臨不測，無所避。

translations.literal: Wen personally supervised laborers in repairing and completing them; though facing the unpredictable, he avoided nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wen personally supervised repairs, facing the danger without flinching.

sentences.zh: 僚屬或止溫，溫曰：「為政疵癘，水泛溢為災，守臣之罪。

translations.literal: Some subordinates tried to stop Wen; Wen said: "When governance has flaws, floods overflowing are a disaster—the fault of the guarding minister.
translations.idiomatic: When subordinates tried to stop him, Wen said: "When governance is flawed, floods are the fault of the local administrator.

sentences.zh: 當以此身為百姓謝，雖死不恨。」

translations.literal: I ought to offer this body in apology to the people—even death would bring no regret."
translations.idiomatic: I should offer my life in apology to the people—I would not regret death."

sentences.zh: 移鎮武定，歲旱且蝗，溫割指，以血瀝酒中，禱而酹之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Wuding; in a year of drought and locusts, Wen cut his finger, let the blood drip into wine, prayed, and poured a libation.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Wuding, during drought and locusts he cut his finger, mixed the blood with wine, and poured a libation in prayer.

sentences.zh: 既而雨沾足，有群鴉啄蝗且盡，由是歲熟，人以為至誠之感雲。

translations.literal: Before long rain fell in abundance; flocks of crows pecked the locusts until nearly all were gone; thereby the year ripened well, and people regarded it as a response to utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Rain soon fell in abundance; crows devoured the locusts; the harvest was good, and people attributed it to his sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 以老致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired on account of age and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in old age and died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：軍旅之事，鋒鏑在前，不計其死。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In military affairs, with blades and arrows before one, one does not reckon with death.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: In warfare, with blades and arrows before one, death is not counted.

sentences.zh: 耳屬金鼓，目屬旌旗，心屬號令，此行列之任也。

translations.literal: The ears attend to gongs and drums, the eyes to banners and flags, the heart to commands—such is the duty of those in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ears heed the drums, eyes the banners, the heart the commands—such is the soldier's duty.

sentences.zh: 自收國用兵，至於大定和宋以前，用命之士，雖細必錄，所以明功也。

translations.literal: From the use of arms in Shouguo down to before the Dading peace with Song, men who gave their lives—even in small matters were recorded, thereby to make merit clear.
translations.idiomatic: From Shouguo through the Dading peace with Song, men who gave their utmost were recorded even in small matters, to make their merit clear.

sentences.zh: 蕭仲恭

translations.literal: Xiao Zhonggong
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhonggong

sentences.zh: 蕭仲恭，本名術里者。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhonggong's original name was Shulizhe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhonggong was born Shulizhe.

sentences.zh: 祖撻不也，仕遼為樞密使，守司徒，封蘭陵郡王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tabuye served Liao as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, held the post of Minister of Education, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tabuye served Liao as commissioner of military affairs, minister of education, and Prince of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 父特末，為中書令，守司空，尚主。

translations.literal: His father Temo was Director of the Secretariat, held the post of Minister of Works, and married an imperial princess.
translations.idiomatic: His father Temo was director of the secretariat, minister of works, and married to an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 仲恭性恭謹，動有禮節，能被甲超橐駝。

translations.literal: Zhonggong's nature was respectful and cautious; in movement he observed ritual propriety, and he could don armor and leap over camels.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful and cautious by nature, he observed ritual propriety in all his conduct and could don armor and leap over camels.

sentences.zh: 遼故事，宗戚子弟別為一班，號「孩兒班」，仲恭嘗為班使，曆宮使、本班詳穩。

translations.literal: By Liao precedent, sons and younger brothers of the imperial clan formed a separate group called the "Children's Company"; Zhonggong once served as company envoy and passed through palace envoy and detailed stability of that company.
translations.idiomatic: By Liao custom, young imperial clansmen formed a separate company called the "Children's Company"; Zhonggong served as its envoy and rose through palace offices.

sentences.zh: 遼帝西奔天德，仲恭為護衛太保，兼領軍事。

translations.literal: When the Liao emperor fled west to Tiande, Zhonggong was Grand Guardian of the Escort and concurrently commanded military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor fled west to Tiande, Zhonggong served as grand guardian of the escort with concurrent military command.

sentences.zh: 至霍里底泊，大軍奄至，倉卒走。

translations.literal: At Huolidipo the main army suddenly arrived and they fled in haste.
translations.idiomatic: At Huolidipo the Jin army suddenly appeared and they fled in haste.

sentences.zh: 仲恭母馬乏，不能進，謂仲恭兄弟曰：「汝等盡節國家，無以我為也。」

translations.literal: Zhonggong's mother's horse was exhausted and could not advance; she said to Zhonggong and his brothers: "You give your full loyalty to the state; do not consider me."
translations.idiomatic: His mother's horse gave out; she told Zhonggong and his brothers: "Serve the state with full loyalty; do not concern yourselves with me."

sentences.zh: 仲恭母，遼道宗季女也。

translations.literal: Zhonggong's mother was a younger daughter of Liao Emperor Daozong.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a younger daughter of Liao Emperor Daozong.

sentences.zh: 遼主傷之，命弟仲宣留侍其母。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler was grieved by this and ordered his younger brother Zhongxuan to remain and attend their mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor, grieved, ordered his younger brother Zhongxuan to stay and attend their mother.

sentences.zh: 仲恭從而西。

translations.literal: Zhonggong followed and went west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggong continued west with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 時大雪，寒甚，遼主乏食，仲恭進衣並進乾糒。

translations.literal: At that time snow was heavy and the cold extreme; the Liao ruler lacked food; Zhonggong presented clothing and also presented dried provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In heavy snow and bitter cold, with the emperor starving, Zhonggong presented clothing and dried provisions.

sentences.zh: 遼主困，仲恭伏冰雪中，遼主藉之以憩。

translations.literal: When the Liao ruler was exhausted, Zhonggong lay in the ice and snow, and the Liao ruler rested upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor collapsed from exhaustion, Zhonggong lay in the snow for him to rest upon.

sentences.zh: 凡六日，乃至天德，始得食。

translations.literal: For six days in all they traveled before reaching Tiande and at last obtained food.
translations.idiomatic: After six days they reached Tiande and at last found food.

sentences.zh: 後與遼主俱獲，太宗以仲恭忠於其主，特加禮待。

translations.literal: Later he and the Liao ruler were both captured; Emperor Taizong, because Zhonggong had been loyal to his lord, treated him with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He and the Liao emperor were both captured; Emperor Taizong honored Zhonggong's loyalty with special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，仲恭使宋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui Zhonggong was envoy to Song.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 4 Zhonggong was sent as envoy to Song.

sentences.zh: 且還，宋人意仲恭、耶律餘睹皆有亡國之戚，而餘睹為監軍，有兵權，可誘而用之，乃以蠟丸書令仲恭致之餘睹，使為內應。

translations.literal: On his return, the Song thought that Zhonggong and Yelü Yudu both bore the sorrow of a fallen state, and that Yudu as supervising general held military authority and could be enticed and used; they therefore sent a wax-sealed letter ordering Zhonggong to deliver it to Yudu to serve as an inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the Song believed Zhonggong and Yelü Yudu, both grieving a fallen state, could be turned—Yudu held military command—and sent a wax-sealed letter for Zhonggong to deliver to Yudu as an inside collaborator.

sentences.zh: 仲恭素忠信，無反覆志，但恐宋人留不遣，遂陽許。

translations.literal: Zhonggong had always been loyal and trustworthy with no intent to turn traitor, but feared the Song would detain him and not let him go, and therefore falsely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal by nature, Zhonggong had no thought of treachery but feared detention by the Song and feigned agreement.

sentences.zh: 還見宗望，即以蠟丸書獻之。

translations.literal: On returning he saw Zongwang and immediately presented the wax-sealed letter.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he presented the wax-sealed letter to Zongwang.

sentences.zh: 宗望察仲恭無他，薄罰之。

translations.literal: Zongwang perceived that Zhonggong had no other intent and lightly punished him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang saw Zhonggong had no treacherous intent and punished him lightly.

sentences.zh: 於是再舉伐宋，執二帝以歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon they campaigned against Song again and brought the two emperors back as captives.
translations.idiomatic: The army then invaded Song again and brought the two emperors back as captives.

sentences.zh: 累遷右宣徽使，改都點檢。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Right Director of the Palace Domestic Service and changed to Chief Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right director of the palace domestic service, then chief inspector.

sentences.zh: 宗磐與宗幹爭辯于熙宗前，宗磐拔刀向宗幹，仲恭呵之乃止。

translations.literal: Zongpan and Zonggan argued before Xizong; Zongpan drew his sword toward Zonggan; Zhonggong shouted at him and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongpan and Zonggan argued before Xizong, Zongpan drew his sword on Zonggan; Zhonggong shouted him down and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 既而宗磐以反罪誅，仲恭衛禁有備，以功加銀青光祿大夫，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zongpan was executed for treason; Zhonggong's guard of the forbidden precincts had been prepared; for this merit he was given the additional rank of Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongpan was executed for treason, Zhonggong's vigilance in guarding the palace earned him silver-glitter grand master of splendid happiness and promotion to right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，封蘭陵郡王，授世襲猛安，進拜平章政事，同監修國史，封濟王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling Commandery, granted a hereditary meng'an, advanced to Grand Councilor of the Secretariat, made co-supervisor of the compilation of the national history, and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lanling, granted a hereditary meng'an command, promoted to grand councilor, made co-supervisor of the national history, and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 詔葬遼豫王于廣甯，仲恭請往會葬，熙宗義而許之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the burial of Liao Prince Yu at Guangning; Zhonggong requested to go attend the funeral, and Xizong approved it as righteous.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao Prince Yu was to be buried at Guangning, Zhonggong asked to attend the funeral, and Xizong graciously permitted it.

sentences.zh: 改行台左丞相。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Chief Councilor of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became left chief councilor of the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居無何，入為尚書右丞相，拜太傅，領三省事，封曹王。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the capital as Right Chief Councilor of the Secretariat, was appointed Grand Tutor, headed the affairs of the Three Departments, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered the capital as right chief councilor, was appointed grand tutor, headed the three departments, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，封越國王，除燕京留守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yue and appointed Military Commissioner of Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yue and appointed military commissioner of Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 海陵親為書，以玉山子賜之。

translations.literal: Hailing personally wrote a letter and bestowed on him a jade mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing wrote to him in his own hand and bestowed a jade mountain ornament.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨，年六十一。

translations.literal: That year he died; he was sixty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 諡貞簡。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Loyal and Simple.

sentences.zh: 正隆例降王爵，改儀同三司、鄭國公。

translations.literal: By Zhenglong precedent his princely rank was reduced; he was changed to Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes and Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhenglong precedent his princely rank was reduced to equal in rank to the three dukes, Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 子拱。

translations.literal: His son was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gong.

sentences.zh: 子 拱

translations.literal: Son: Gong
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong

sentences.zh: 拱本名迪輦阿不，初為蘭子山猛安。

translations.literal: Gong's original name was Dilianabu; he was first meng'an of Lanzishan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, born Dilianabu, was first meng'an commander of Lanzishan.

sentences.zh: 海陵為宰相，徼取人譽，薦大臣子以為達官，遂以拱為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Hailing was grand councilor he sought people's praise, recommending sons of great ministers for high office; thus Gong was made Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was grand councilor he sought reputation by promoting sons of great ministers; Gong was made vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 耶律彌勒，拱妻女弟也，海陵將納為妃，使拱自汴取之。

translations.literal: Yelü Mile was the younger sister of Gong's wife; Hailing was about to take her as consort and had Gong fetch her from Bian himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Mile, younger sister of Gong's wife, was to be taken as consort; Hailing sent Gong to fetch her from Bian.

sentences.zh: 還過燕，是時仲恭為燕京留守，見彌勒身形不類處子，竊憂之，曰：「上多猜嫌，拱其及禍矣。」

translations.literal: On the return he passed through Yan; at that time Zhonggong was military commissioner of Yanjing; seeing Mile's figure unlike a maiden's, he privately worried and said: "The emperor is much given to suspicion—Gong may meet with disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Yan, where Zhonggong was military commissioner, he saw Mile's figure was not that of a maiden and privately feared: "The emperor is suspicious—Gong may come to harm."

sentences.zh: 拱去不數日，仲恭卒。

translations.literal: Within a few days of Gong's departure, Zhonggong died.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of Gong's departure, Zhonggong died.

sentences.zh: 拱至上京，聞訃，以本官起複，佩信牌，往燕京治葬事。

translations.literal: When Gong reached the Upper Capital and heard the death announcement, he was recalled from mourning to his former post, wore the credential tablet, and went to Yanjing to manage funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the Upper Capital Gong heard of his father's death, was recalled from mourning, and went to Yanjing with his credential tablet to manage the funeral.

sentences.zh: 未行，彌勒入宮，果如仲恭所相度，即遣出宮。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Mile entered the palace; it was indeed as Zhonggong had judged, and she was immediately sent out of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Mile entered the palace; as Zhonggong had feared, she was immediately sent out.

sentences.zh: 夜半召拱至禁中，詰問無狀。

translations.literal: At midnight Gong was summoned to the forbidden precincts and interrogated; there was no evidence.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Gong was summoned to the palace and interrogated; no evidence was found.

sentences.zh: 海陵終疑之，乃罷拱禮部侍郎，奪其信牌。

translations.literal: Hailing ultimately remained suspicious; he thereupon dismissed Gong from Vice Minister of Rites and stripped him of his credential tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing remained suspicious, dismissed Gong from vice minister of rites, and stripped him of his credential tablet.

sentences.zh: 拱待命，逾年不報，歸蘭子山治猛安事。

translations.literal: Gong awaited orders; for more than a year there was no response; he returned to Lanzishan to manage meng'an affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gong waited over a year without word and returned to Lanzishan to manage his meng'an command.

sentences.zh: 是時，蕭恭、張九坐語禁中事得罪，拱至蘭子山，與客會語及之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Gong and Zhang Jiu had been punished for speaking of affairs within the forbidden precincts; when Gong reached Lanzishan, he discussed this with guests at a gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Gong and Zhang Jiu had been punished for discussing palace affairs; at Lanzishan Gong spoke of this with guests.

sentences.zh: 有阿納與拱有隙，乃誣拱言張九無罪被誅，語涉怨謗。

translations.literal: One Ana bore a grudge against Gong and falsely accused him of saying that Zhang Jiu was executed though guiltless, his words involving resentment and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Ana, who bore a grudge against Gong, accused him of saying Zhang Jiu was executed though innocent, with words of resentment and slander.

sentences.zh: 海陵遣使鞫之，戒使者曰：「此子狂妄，宜有此語，不然彼中安得知此事。」

translations.literal: Hailing dispatched an envoy to interrogate him and warned the envoy: "This fellow is arrogant and reckless—he ought to have said such things; otherwise how could they there know of this matter?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent an interrogator with instructions: "This man is reckless—he must have said such things; otherwise how could they know of this there?"

sentences.zh: 使者不復問拱，但榜掠其左驗，使如告語證之，拱遂見殺。

translations.literal: The envoy did not question Gong further but only flogged his left thigh to make the confession match the accusation; Gong was thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy did not question Gong but flogged him until he confessed as accused; Gong was executed.

sentences.zh: 蕭仲宣

translations.literal: Xiao Zhongxuan
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhongxuan

sentences.zh: 仲宣，本名野里補，仲恭母弟。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's original name was Yelibu; he was Zhonggong's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan, born Yelibu, was Zhonggong's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 聰敏好學，沉厚少言。

translations.literal: He was intelligent and quick, fond of learning, deep and steady, and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent and fond of learning, he was deep, steady, and sparing of speech.

sentences.zh: 五歲，遙授郡刺史，累加太子少師，為本班詳穩。

translations.literal: At age five he was appointed from afar as Prefect of a commandery, was promoted in succession to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and became detailed stability of his company.
translations.idiomatic: At five he was remotely appointed prefect of a commandery, rose to junior mentor to the heir apparent, and became detailed stability of his company.

sentences.zh: 從天祚西，為護衛太保左右班詳穩。

translations.literal: He followed Tianzuo west and became detailed stability of the left and right companies under the Grand Guardian of the Escort.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Tianzuo west and served as detailed stability of the escort guard's left and right companies.

sentences.zh: 至石輦鐸，遼主留仲宣侍母，遂與其母皆見獲。

translations.literal: At Shinian Duo the Liao ruler left Zhongxuan to attend his mother; he and his mother were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: At Shinian Duo the Liao emperor left Zhongxuan to attend their mother; both mother and son were captured.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，且謂仲宣能知遼國故事，命權宣徽使，從睿宗伐康王。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong praised this and moreover said Zhongxuan knew Liao state precedents; he was ordered to act as Director of the Palace Domestic Service and followed Prince Rui in campaigning against Prince Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong commended him and, noting his knowledge of Liao precedents, appointed him acting director of the palace domestic service and sent him with Prince Rui against Prince Kang.

sentences.zh: 師還，家居者久之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he remained at home for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he remained at home for many years.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，特授鎮國上將軍，曆順義、永定、昭義、武甯四鎮節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he was specially appointed General Who Guards the State and passed through military commissioner of the four garrisons Shunyi, Yongding, Zhaoyi, and Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 2 he was specially appointed general who guards the state and served as military commissioner of Shunyi, Yongding, Zhaoyi, and Wuning in succession.

sentences.zh: 為政平易，小吏不敢為奸。

translations.literal: His governance was easy and fair; petty clerks did not dare commit wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was fair and straightforward; petty clerks dared not commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 賄賂禁絕，奴婢入郡，人莫識其面。

translations.literal: Bribery was entirely forbidden; when slaves and servants entered the prefecture, people did not know their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Bribery was forbidden; when his servants entered the prefecture, no one knew their faces.

sentences.zh: 朔、潞百姓皆為立祠刻石頌之。

translations.literal: The common people of Shuo and Lu all erected shrines and carved stone inscriptions to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shuo and Lu erected shrines and carved stone inscriptions in his honor.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenglong 2 at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 高松，本名檀朵，澄州析木人。

translations.literal: Gao Song, original name Tanduo, was a man of Ximu in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Song, born Tanduo, was a native of Ximu in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 年十九，從軍為蒲輦，有力善戰，宗弼聞其名，召置左右，從破汴京及和尚原，累官咸平總管府判官。

translations.literal: At age nineteen he joined the army as a puyan; powerful and skilled in battle, when Zongbi heard his name he summoned him and placed him at his side; he followed in the capture of Bianjing and Heshangyuan and was promoted in succession to Judicial Aide of the Xianping Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he joined the army as a puyan; powerful and skilled in battle, Zongbi summoned him to his side; he fought at Bianjing and Heshangyuan and rose to judicial aide of the Xianping commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，充管押東京路渤海萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he served as overseer of the Bohai ten-thousand-household command of the Eastern Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he oversaw the Bohai ten-thousand-household command of the Eastern Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書可喜謀反，前同知延安尹李老僧曰：「我與萬戶高松謀之，必從我矣。」

translations.literal: Minister of War Kexi plotted rebellion; the former Vice Administrator of Yan'an Li Laoseng said: "If I plot with the ten-thousand-household commander Gao Song, he will surely follow me."
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Kexi plotted rebellion, the former vice administrator of Yan'an Li Laoseng said: "If I win over Ten-Thousand-Household Commander Gao Song, he will surely join me."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「若得此軍，舉事易矣。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "If we obtain this army, raising the affair will be easy."
translations.idiomatic: The others said: "With that army, the undertaking will be easy."

sentences.zh: 老僧往見松，說松曰：「君有功舊人，至今不得大官，何也？」

translations.literal: Laoseng went to see Song and persuaded him, saying: "You are a man of old merit—why have you still not received high office?"
translations.idiomatic: Laoseng went to Song and said: "You are a man of old merit—why have you never received high office?"

sentences.zh: 松曰：「我一縣令也，每念聖恩，累世不能報，尚敢有望乎！」

translations.literal: Song said: "I am but a county magistrate; I constantly recall the sage's grace—for generations we could not repay it—how would I still dare to harbor expectations!"
translations.idiomatic: Song replied: "I am but a county magistrate. I constantly recall the emperor's grace—my family could never repay it in generations—how dare I harbor such ambitions!"

sentences.zh: 老僧遂不敢言。

translations.literal: Laoseng thereupon did not dare speak further.
translations.idiomatic: Laoseng dared speak no further.

sentences.zh: 可喜、布輝、阿瑣知事不可成，遂上變，共捕斡論赴有司。

translations.literal: Kexi, Buhui, and Asuo knew the affair could not succeed and thereupon reported the plot; together they captured Wolun and delivered him to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Kexi, Buhui, and Asuo, seeing the plot could not succeed, reported it and together captured Wolun and delivered him to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 松從征窩斡，以功遷咸平少尹，四遷崇義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Song followed the campaign against Wowo; for merit he was transferred to Junior Administrator of Xianping and was four times transferred to Military Commissioner of the Chongyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Song campaigned against Wowo; for his service he became junior administrator of Xianping, then military commissioner of the Chongyi Army after four transfers.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：忠信行己，豈不大哉！

translations.literal: The encomium says: To conduct oneself with loyalty and trustworthiness—is this not great!
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: To live by loyalty and trustworthiness—is that not greatness itself!

sentences.zh: 蕭仲恭盡心故主，而富貴福澤向之，與宗室舊臣等矣。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhonggong gave his full heart to his former lord, yet wealth, honor, and blessings turned toward him, equal to the old ministers of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhonggong gave his full devotion to his former lord, yet wealth and honor came to him equal to the old ministers of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 仲恭廷叱宗磐而朝廷尊，高松誼遏李老僧而社稷安，皆有古烈丈夫之風焉。

translations.literal: Zhonggong rebuked Zongpan in court and the court was honored; Gao Song by righteousness checked Li Laoseng and the altars of state were secure—both had the bearing of great stalwart men of old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggong rebuked Zongpan in court and preserved the court's dignity; Gao Song by moral force checked Li Laoseng and secured the state—both had the bearing of great men of old.

sentences.zh: 海陵諸子

translations.literal: The Sons of Hailing
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Emperor Hailing

sentences.zh: 海陵後徒單氏生太子光英，元妃大氏生崇王元壽，柔妃唐括氏生宿王矧思阿補，才人南氏生滕王廣陽。

translations.literal: Hailing's empress the Tushan clan bore the crown prince Guangying; primary consort the Da clan bore Prince Chong Yuanshou; Gentle Consort the Tangguo clan bore Prince Su Shensi Abu; Talented Lady the Nan clan bore Prince Teng Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Tushan bore Crown Prince Guangying; Primary Consort Da bore Prince Chong Yuanshou; Gentle Consort Tangguo bore Prince Su Shensi Abu; Talented Lady Nan bore Prince Teng Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 光英本名阿魯補，徒單後所生。

translations.literal: Guangying's original name was Alubu; he was born of the Tushan empress.
translations.idiomatic: Guangying, born Alubu, was the son of Empress Tushan.

sentences.zh: 是時燕京轉運使趙襲慶多男，故又名曰趙六。

translations.literal: At that time the Yanjing transport commissioner Zhao Xiqing had many sons, and so he was also named Zhao Six.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanjing transport commissioner Zhao Xiqing had many sons, so the prince was also nicknamed Zhao Six.

sentences.zh: 養于同判大宗正方之家，故崇德大夫沈璋妻張氏嘗為光英保母，於是贈璋銀青光祿大夫，賜宗正方錢千萬。

translations.literal: He was raised in the household of Associate Judge of the Great Clan Zongzheng; thus the Honored Virtue Grandee Shen Zhang's wife Lady Zhang had once been Guangying's nurse; thereupon Zhang was posthumously granted Silver-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Zongzheng was given ten million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the household of Associate Judge Zongzheng of the Great Clan, Shen Zhang's wife Lady Zhang had been his nurse; Zhang was posthumously granted silver-glitter grand master of splendid happiness and Zongzheng was given ten million cash.

sentences.zh: 天德四年二月，立光英為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Tiande, Guangying was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tiande 4, Guangying was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 是月，安置太祖畫像于武德殿，盡召國初嘗從太祖破甯江州有功者，得百七十六人，並加宣武將軍，賜酒帛。

translations.literal: That month, Taizu's portrait was installed in Wude Hall; all who in the founding of the state had followed Taizu in capturing Ningjiangzhou with merit were summoned—one hundred seventy-six men were found—and all were given the rank of Martial Proclamation General and bestowed wine and silks.
translations.idiomatic: That month Taizu's portrait was installed in Wude Hall; all who had fought with Taizu at Ningjiangzhou in the founding era were summoned—176 men—and all were granted the rank of martial proclamation general and given wine and silk.

sentences.zh: 其中有忽里罕者，解其衣進光英曰：「臣今年百歲矣，有子十人。

translations.literal: Among them was one Hulihan, who removed his garment and presented it to Guangying, saying: "Your servant is one hundred years old this year and has ten sons.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was Hulihan, who removed his garment and presented it to Guangying, saying: "I am a hundred years old this year and have ten sons.

sentences.zh: 願太子壽考多男子與小臣等。」

translations.literal: I wish the crown prince long life and many sons like your humble servant and his."
translations.idiomatic: I wish the crown prince long life and many sons, like me and mine."

sentences.zh: 海陵使光英受其衣，海陵即以所服並佩刀賜忽里罕，答其厚意。

translations.literal: Hailing had Guangying accept his garment; Hailing then bestowed on Hulihan what he himself wore and his belt sword, repaying his deep sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had Guangying accept the garment, then bestowed his own robes and sword on Hulihan in return for the old man's devotion.

sentences.zh: 後以「英」字與「鷹隼」字聲相近，改「鷹坊」為「馴鷙坊」。

translations.literal: Later, because the character "ying" was close in sound to "ying" in "hawk and falcon," the "Hawk Workshop" was changed to the "Tamed Hawk Workshop."
translations.idiomatic: Later, because the character ying in Guangying's name sounded like ying in "hawk and falcon," the Hawk Workshop was renamed the Tamed Hawk Workshop.

sentences.zh: 國號有「英國」又有「應國」，遂改「英國」為「壽國」，「應國」為「杞國」。

translations.literal: Among state names there were "Ying State" and also "Ying State"; therefore "Ying State" was changed to "Shou State" and "Ying State" to "Qi State."
translations.idiomatic: Because there were states named Ying and Ying (homophones), the former was renamed Shou and the latter Qi.

sentences.zh: 宋亦改「光州」為「蔣州」，「光山縣」為「期思縣」，「光化軍」為「通化軍」雲。

translations.literal: Song also changed "Guangzhou" to "Jiangzhou," "Guangshan County" to "Qisi County," and "Guanghua Army" to "Tonghua Army," and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Song likewise renamed Guangzhou to Jiangzhou, Guangshan County to Qisi County, and Guanghua Army to Tonghua Army.

sentences.zh: 正隆元年三月二十七日，光英生日，宴百官于神龍殿，賜京師大酺一日。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the third month of the first year of Zhenglong, Guangying's birthday, officials were feasted in the Divine Dragon Hall and the capital was granted a grand communal feast for one day.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day of the third month of Zhenglong 1, Guangying's birthday, officials were feasted in the Divine Dragon Hall and the capital was granted a day of public celebration.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，光英射鴉，獲之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year, Guangying shot a crow and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year Guangying shot and killed a crow.

sentences.zh: 海陵大喜，命薦原廟，賜光英馬一匹，黃金三斤，班賜從者有差。

translations.literal: Hailing was greatly pleased, ordered it offered at the original temple, bestowed on Guangying one horse and three jin of gold, and distributed rewards to followers in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was delighted, ordered offerings at the ancestral temple, gave Guangying a horse and three jin of gold, and rewarded his attendants in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年，海陵行幸南京，次安肅州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong, Hailing traveled to the Southern Capital and halted at Ansu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 6 Hailing traveled to the Southern Capital and halted at Ansu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 光英獲二兔，遣使薦于山陵。

translations.literal: Guangying obtained two hares and dispatched envoys to offer them at the mountain tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangying caught two hares and sent envoys to offer them at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 居數日，複獲麞兔，從官皆稱賀。

translations.literal: After several days he again obtained deer and hares; the attending officials all offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he caught deer and hares again, and the attending officials all offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 賜光英名馬弓矢，複遣使薦于山陵。

translations.literal: He bestowed on Guangying famous horses, bows, and arrows, and again dispatched envoys to offer at the mountain tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Guangying fine horses, bows, and arrows, and again sent offerings to the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 六月，海陵至南京，群臣迎謁，海陵與徒單後、光英共載而入。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Hailing reached the Southern Capital; the ministers came to welcome and pay respects; Hailing entered riding together with the Tushan empress and Guangying.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Hailing reached the Southern Capital; the ministers welcomed him, and he entered the city riding with Empress Tushan and Guangying.

sentences.zh: 海陵嘗言：「俟太子年十八，以天下付之。

translations.literal: Hailing once said: "When the crown prince reaches eighteen, I shall entrust the realm to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing once said: "When the crown prince turns eighteen, I shall entrust the realm to him.

sentences.zh: 朕當日游宴于宮掖苑囿中以自娛樂。」

translations.literal: I shall then pass my days feasting and roaming in the palace quarters and gardens for my own pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: I shall spend my days feasting and roaming in the palace gardens for my own pleasure."

sentences.zh: 光英頗警悟，海陵謂侍臣曰：「上智不學而能，中性未有不由學而成者。

translations.literal: Guangying was quite quick-witted; Hailing said to attending ministers: "The highest intelligence needs no study to achieve ability; those of middling nature have none who do not become accomplished through study.
translations.idiomatic: Guangying was quick-witted; Hailing told his ministers: "The highest intelligence needs no study; those of middling nature achieve nothing without it.

sentences.zh: 太子宜擇碩德宿學之士，使輔導之，庶知古今，防過失。

translations.literal: The crown prince should select men of great virtue and long learning to instruct and guide him, so that he may know past and present and guard against faults.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince should have men of great virtue and learning to instruct him, that he may know past and present and guard against error.

sentences.zh: 詩文小技，何必作耶。

translations.literal: Poetry and prose are petty skills—why must he compose them?
translations.idiomatic: Poetry and prose are petty skills—why trouble with them?

sentences.zh: 至於騎射之事，亦不可不習，恐其懦柔也。」

translations.literal: As for horsemanship and archery, he also must not fail to practice them, lest he become timid and soft."
translations.idiomatic: Horsemanship and archery must also be practiced, lest he grow timid and soft."

sentences.zh: 及將親征，後與光英挽衣號慟，海陵亦泣下曰：「吾行歸矣。」

translations.literal: When he was about to campaign in person, the empress and Guangying clutched his robes and wailed; Hailing also wept and said: "I shall return."
translations.idiomatic: When he prepared to campaign in person, the empress and Guangying clutched his robes and wept; Hailing wept as well and said: "I shall return."

sentences.zh: 後誦《孝經》。

translations.literal: The empress recited the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was reading the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 一日，忽謂人曰：「《經》言三千之罪，莫大于不孝，何為不孝？」

translations.literal: One day she suddenly said to someone: "The classic says that among three thousand offenses none is greater than unfilial conduct—what is unfilial conduct?"
translations.idiomatic: One day she suddenly asked: "The classic says that among three thousand offenses none is greater than unfilial conduct—what counts as unfilial?"

sentences.zh: 對者曰：「今民家子博弈飲酒，不養父母，皆不孝也。」

translations.literal: The respondent said: "Nowadays common people's sons gamble and drink and do not support their parents—all this is unfilial."
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "When sons gamble and drink and fail to support their parents—that is unfilial conduct."

sentences.zh: 光英默然良久，曰：「此豈足為不孝耶！」

translations.literal: Guangying was silent for a long while and said: "How could this be enough to count as unfilial!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangying was silent a long while, then said: "Surely that is not what counts as unfilial!"

sentences.zh: 蓋指言海陵弑母事。

translations.literal: This was plainly an allusion to Hailing's murder of his mother.
translations.idiomatic: This was plainly an allusion to Hailing's murder of his mother.

sentences.zh: 及伐宋，光英居守，以陀滿訛里也為太子少師兼河南路統軍使，以衛護之。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Song, Guangying remained to guard the capital; Tuoman Eliye was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Circuit to protect and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Song began, Guangying remained as regent; Tuoman Eliye was appointed junior mentor to the heir apparent and commander of the Henan circuit to protect him.

sentences.zh: 完顏元宜軍變，海陵遇害，都督府移文訛里也，殺光英於汴京，死時年十二。

translations.literal: Wanyan Yuanyi mutinied; Hailing was killed; the commandery office sent a dispatch to Eliye, and Guangying was killed at Bianjing; at death he was twelve years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanyan Yuanyi's army mutinied and Hailing was killed, headquarters ordered Eliye to kill Guangying at Bianjing; he was twelve.

sentences.zh: 後與海陵俱葬于大房山諸王墓次。

translations.literal: Later he was buried together with Hailing in the tomb precinct of the princes at Dafang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He was later buried with Hailing in the princes' tombs at Mount Dafang.

sentences.zh: 訛里也，咸平路窟吐忽河人，襲其父忽土猛安。

translations.literal: Eliye was a man of Kutuhuhe on the Xianping Circuit and inherited his father Hutu's meng'an command.
translations.idiomatic: Eliye, from Kutuhuhe on the Xianping Circuit, inherited his father Hutu's meng'an command.

sentences.zh: 除邳州刺史，三遷昌武軍節度使、歸德尹、南京留守、河南路統軍使、太子少師。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Pizhou, was thrice transferred to Military Commissioner of the Changwu Army, Administrator of Guide, Military Commissioner of the Southern Capital, Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Circuit, and Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Pizhou, then military commissioner of the Changwu Army, administrator of Guide, military commissioner of the Southern Capital, commander of the Henan circuit, and junior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，遷元帥右都監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was transferred to Right Supervising Commissioner of the Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 he was promoted to right supervising commissioner of the marshal.

sentences.zh: 宋人陷陳、蔡，訛里也師久無功，已而兵敗于宋，解職。

translations.literal: When Song captured Chen and Cai, Eliye's army for a long time achieved no merit; soon afterward the army was defeated by Song and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Song captured Chen and Cai, Eliye's army achieved nothing for a long time, then was defeated; he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 俄起為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to serve as Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂之曰：「卿為河南統軍，門多私謁，百姓惡之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said to him: "When you were commander-in-chief of Henan, your gate was full of private callers and the common people hated it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong told him: "As commander of Henan your gate was crowded with private callers and the people resented it.

sentences.zh: 其後經略陳、蔡，不惟無功，且複致敗。

translations.literal: Afterward in operations against Chen and Cai you not only achieved no merit but again brought defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning against Chen and Cai, you achieved nothing and brought defeat.

sentences.zh: 以汝舊勞，故複用汝。

translations.literal: Because of your old service I employ you again.
translations.idiomatic: Because of your old service I employ you again.

sentences.zh: 京兆地近南邊，宜善理之。」

translations.literal: Jingzhao lies near the southern frontier—you should govern it well."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao lies near the southern frontier—govern it well."

sentences.zh: 大定三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dading 3.

sentences.zh: 元壽，天德元年封崇王。

translations.literal: Yuanshou was enfeoffed as Prince Chong in the first year of Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshou was enfeoffed as Prince Chong in Tiande 1.

sentences.zh: 三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year.

sentences.zh: 矧思阿補

translations.literal: Shensi Abu
translations.idiomatic: Shensi Abu

sentences.zh: 矧思阿補，正隆元年四月生。

translations.literal: Shensi Abu was born in the fourth month of the first year of Zhenglong.
translations.idiomatic: Shensi Abu was born in the fourth month of Zhenglong 1.

sentences.zh: 小底東勝家保養之，賜東勝錢千萬，仍為起第。

translations.literal: The petty official Dongsheng's household raised and nurtured him; Dongsheng was given ten million in cash and a residence was built for him.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised in the household of the attendant Dongsheng, who was given ten million cash and a residence was built for him.

sentences.zh: 五月已酉，彌月，封其母唐括氏為柔妃，賜京師貧者五千人錢，人錢二百。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day of the fifth month, at the full month, his mother the Tangguo clan was enfeoffed as Gentle Consort; five thousand poor persons of the capital were given cash, two hundred per person.
translations.idiomatic: At his first-month celebration his mother Lady Tangguo was enfeoffed as Gentle Consort, and five thousand poor persons in the capital each received two hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 二年，矧思阿補生日，海陵與永壽太后及皇后、太子光英幸東勝家。

translations.literal: In the second year, on Shensi Abu's birthday, Hailing with the Yongshou empress dowager, the empress, and Crown Prince Guangying visited Dongsheng's household.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on Shensi Abu's birthday, Hailing visited Dongsheng's home with the Yongshou empress dowager, the empress, and Crown Prince Guangying.

sentences.zh: 三年正月五日，矧思阿補薨。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year, Shensi Abu died.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Shensi Abu died.

sentences.zh: 海陵殺太醫副使謝友正、醫者安宗義及其乳母，杖東勝一百，除名。

translations.literal: Hailing killed Vice Director of the Imperial Physicians Xie Youzheng, the physician An Zongyi, and his wet nurse; Dongsheng was flogged one hundred strokes and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing executed Vice Director of Physicians Xie Youzheng, physician An Zongyi, and the wet nurse; Dongsheng received a hundred strokes and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 明日，追封矧思阿補為宿王，葬大房山。

translations.literal: The next day Shensi Abu was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Su and buried at Dafang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shensi Abu was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Su and buried at Mount Dafang.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫楊伯雄入直禁中，因與同直者相語，伯雄曰：「宿王之死，蓋養于宮外，供護雖謹，不若父母膝下。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Grandee Yang Boxiong entered duty in the forbidden precincts and, conversing with a fellow on duty, Boxiong said: "Prince Su's death—he was raised outside the palace; though care and protection were careful, it was not like being at his parents' knees.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Grandee Yang Boxiong, on duty in the palace, said to a colleague: "Prince Su's death—raised outside the palace, however carefully tended, is not the same as at a parent's knee.

sentences.zh: 豈國家風俗素尚如此。」

translations.literal: Could it be that the state's customs have always valued this?"
translations.idiomatic: Has the state always valued such custom?"

sentences.zh: 或以此言告海陵。

translations.literal: Someone reported these words to Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported this to Hailing.

sentences.zh: 海陵大怒，謂伯雄曰：「爾臣子也，君父所為，豈得言風俗。

translations.literal: Hailing was greatly enraged and said to Boxiong: "You are a subject—how can you speak of customs regarding what ruler and father do?
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was furious and said to Boxiong: "You are a subject—how dare you speak of customs regarding what your ruler does?

sentences.zh: 宮禁中事，豈爾當言。

translations.literal: Affairs within the palace forbidden precincts—how are they for you to speak of?
translations.idiomatic: Palace affairs are not yours to discuss.

sentences.zh: 朕或體中不佳，間不視朝，只是少得人幾拜耳。

translations.literal: When I am unwell in body and occasionally do not hold court, it is only that a few fewer people bow—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: When I am unwell and occasionally miss court, it only means a few fewer bows—that is all.

sentences.zh: 而庶事皆奏決便殿，縱有死刑不即論決，蓋使囚者得緩其死。

translations.literal: Yet all routine affairs are reported and decided in the convenient hall; even when there is capital punishment it is not immediately decided, so that prisoners may have their death delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all routine business is decided in the side hall; even capital cases are not decided at once, giving prisoners a reprieve.

sentences.zh: 至於除授宣敕雖複稽緩，有何利害。

translations.literal: As for appointments and edicts of authorization, though they are again slow, what harm is there?
translations.idiomatic: As for appointments and edicts, though they may be slow, what harm is there?

sentences.zh: 朕每當閒暇，頗閱教坊聲樂，聊以自娛。

translations.literal: Whenever I have leisure I quite often enjoy the music of the instruction quarter, simply to amuse myself.
translations.idiomatic: In my leisure I enjoy music from the instruction quarter simply to amuse myself.

sentences.zh: 《書》雲：'內作色荒，外作禽荒，酣酒嗜音，峻宇雕牆，有一於此，未或不亡。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'Within, making lust a wasteland; without, making hunting a wasteland; deep drinking and love of sound; lofty halls and carved walls—if there is one of these, none fails to perish.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: 'Within, making lust a wasteland; without, making hunting a wasteland; deep drinking and love of sound; lofty halls and carved walls—if there is one of these, none fails to perish.'

sentences.zh: '此戒人君不恤國事溺於此者耳。

translations.literal: This warns rulers who do not care for state affairs but drown in such things.
translations.idiomatic: That warns rulers who neglect state affairs and drown in such pleasures.

sentences.zh: 如我雖使聲樂喧動天地，宰相敢有濫與人官而吏敢有受賕者乎。

translations.literal: As for me, though I let music and song shake heaven and earth, would the chief councilor dare indiscriminately to give people office, or clerks dare to accept bribes?
translations.idiomatic: Though I let music shake heaven and earth, would the chief councilor dare give offices indiscriminately, or clerks dare accept bribes?

sentences.zh: 外間敢有竊議者乎。

translations.literal: Would anyone outside dare whisper in private?
translations.idiomatic: Would anyone outside dare whisper criticism?

sentences.zh: 爾諫官也，有可言之事，當公言之。

translations.literal: You are a remonstrating official; when there are matters that may be spoken, you should speak them openly.
translations.idiomatic: You are a remonstrating official; speak openly when there is cause.

sentences.zh: 言而不從，朕之非也。

translations.literal: If you speak and I do not follow, the fault is mine.
translations.idiomatic: If you speak and I do not heed, the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 而乃私議，可乎？」

translations.literal: Yet to discuss in private—how can that be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: But to discuss in private—how is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 伯雄對曰：「陛下至德明聖，固無竊議者。

translations.literal: Boxiong replied: "Your Majesty's utmost virtue is bright and sage—assuredly there are none who whisper in private.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong replied: "Your Majesty's virtue is supreme—assuredly none whisper in private.

sentences.zh: 愚臣失言，罪當萬死，惟陛下哀憐。」

translations.literal: Your foolish servant misspoke; the offense deserves ten thousand deaths—only may Your Majesty show pity."
translations.idiomatic: Your foolish servant misspoke and deserves death—only beg Your Majesty's mercy."

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「本欲殺汝，今只杖汝二百。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "I originally intended to kill you; now I will only flog you two hundred strokes."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said: "I meant to kill you; now I will only flog you two hundred strokes."

sentences.zh: 既決杖至四十，使近臣傳詔諭伯雄曰：「以爾籓邸有舊，今特釋之。」

translations.literal: When the flogging had reached forty strokes, he had a close minister convey an edict telling Boxiong: "Because of your old ties in the princely residence, I now specially release you."
translations.idiomatic: After forty strokes a close minister conveyed an edict: "Because of your old ties in the princely residence, you are specially released."

sentences.zh: 滕王廣陽，母南氏，本大抃家婢，隨元妃大氏入宮，海陵幸之，及有娠，即命為殿直。

translations.literal: Prince Teng Guangyang's mother was the Nan clan, originally a slave girl in Dabian's household; she entered the palace with Primary Consort the Da clan; Hailing favored her, and when she became pregnant he immediately ordered her made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Teng Guangyang's mother Lady Nan was originally a slave in Dabian's household; she entered the palace with Primary Consort Da; when Hailing favored her and she became pregnant, she was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年九月二十六日，生廣陽。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month of the second year of Zhenglong, Guangyang was born.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyang was born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month of Zhenglong 2.

sentences.zh: 十月滿月，海陵分施在京貧民，凡用錢千貫。

translations.literal: At the full month in the tenth month, Hailing distributed gifts among the poor of the capital, using one thousand strings of cash in all.
translations.idiomatic: At his first-month celebration Hailing distributed a thousand strings of cash among the poor of the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，封南氏為才人。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year the Nan clan was enfeoffed as Talented Lady.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year Lady Nan was enfeoffed as Talented Lady.

sentences.zh: 七月，封廣陽為滕王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Guangyang was enfeoffed as Prince Teng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Guangyang was enfeoffed as Prince Teng.

sentences.zh: 九月，薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：海陵伐宋，光英居守，使陀滿訛里也以宮師兼統軍之任，計至悉也，豈料死其手乎。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When Hailing campaigned against Song, Guangying remained to guard the capital; he made Tuoman Eliye bear the duties of palace tutor and concurrently commander-in-chief—the plan was thorough indeed; who could have foreseen death at his hands?
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: When Hailing campaigned against Song, Guangying remained as regent with Tuoman Eliye as tutor and commander—a thorough plan indeed; who could have foreseen death at his hands?

sentences.zh: 荀首有言：「不以人子，吾子其可得耶？」

translations.literal: Xun Shou once said: "If one does not use another's son, can one's own son be obtained?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun Shou once said: "If one does not use another man's son, can one's own son be obtained?"

sentences.zh: 海陵睨人之子不翅魚肉，而獨己子之謀安，不可得矣。

translations.literal: Yet Hailing looked on others' sons as no more than fish and meat on the block, while seeking security for his own son alone—this could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hailing treated other men's sons as meat on the chopping block while scheming safety for his own alone—such an end was impossible.
